Among the perfection of His arrangement is that He made the provision of the servants come through their own labour, as a bounty for them, and made their fodder from what exceeds their need, which they cannot eat. These attributes indicate with certainty that He, glory be to Him, does not err and does not forget, in that He, exalted is He, originated this world comprehensive of everything that its inhabitants need, for the purpose for which He created them: the journey toward Him and the presentation before Him, in all their changing states, in their varying kinds, their differing qualities, and their multiplicity, and the diversity of their temperaments. He left nothing of that lacking, unlike others, (p-298) for if one makes something and strives with all his effort to perfect it, a flaw will inevitably appear in it, and he will keep working to remove it, time after time.

When He had completed this upright proof, indicating the All-Knowing, the All-Wise, he said, alerting to the spread of His lights and the greatness of His station, emphasizing it to counter the deniers: ﴿Indeed in that﴾, that is, in the creation in these various aspects, ﴿are signs﴾ of its Creator, ﴿for people of understanding﴾, the intellects whose nature it is to restrain their possessor from error. As for one who is blind to this, he has no intellect at all, for his intellect has not benefited him, and what does not benefit is in the position of non-existence.

Ibn Kathir mentioned here what Ibn Ishaq attributed in the Sirah (biography of the Prophet) to Zayd ibn 'Amr ibn Nufayl, and Ibn Hisham attributed to Umayya ibn Abi al-Salt:

*And you are the one who, by grace of bounty and mercy, sent to Moses a messenger calling out,*

*So you said: "Go, and Aaron, and call to God Pharaoh, the one who was tyrannical."*

*Say to him: "Did you level this [earth] without a peg, until it stood firm as it is?*

*And say to him: "Did you raise this [sky] without pillars? Be gentle then, as its builder."*

*And say to him: "Did you set its middle, a shining one that guides when night covers it?*

*And say to him: "Who brings out the sun in the morning, so that it makes whatever the crops have touched wither?*

*And say to him: "Who makes the grain grow in the earth, so that from it springs the herb, quivering and swelling?*

*And brings forth from it its grain in its heads; and in that are signs for whoever has understanding."*

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 20, verse 55:

When Allah, glorified and exalted is He, had informed of what He created in the earth of benefits indicating the perfection of His knowledge and the dazzling (bahir) power of His might, in a manner indicating the specific power over resurrection (al-ba'th) [and among the philosophers, the transmigrationists (tanasukhiyya) and others, there were those who acknowledged Allah's oneness (wahdaniyya) but did not affirm the saying of the People of Islam: that the soul (ruh) is a subtle body which permeates the body as fire permeates coal, but rather they say: it is not a body, nor a power in a body, nor a form of a body, and it is not connected to it by the connection of impression (intiba') nor by indwelling (hulul) in it, but by the connection of management (tadbir) and disposal (tasarruf); and that when it departs the body, it joins the spiritual beings of the intelligible world, which is the world of the immaterial (mujarradat), and is enrolled in the thread of the near angels; or it connects with some celestial bodies, such as a star or other, as its connection with the first body, and its attachment to it is severed, so it does not return to it, not even on the Day of Resurrection according to those among them who affirm gathering (hashr)], he connected to that His saying [exalted is He, refuting them, expressing with the pronoun by which the assembled structure (haykal) of body and soul is expressed]: ﴿From it﴾ [i.e., from the earth, not from anything else] ﴿We created you﴾, when We brought you out from it with the dazzling greatness in the first creation, by the creation of your father Adam, upon him be peace; ﴿and into it﴾ [not into anything else, as you are thus observed] ﴿We return you﴾ by death [thus, bodies and souls], so you become dust as you were; [and for the soul, despite that it is in the highest levels (illiyyin), there is in any case some attachment to its body, by which the body perceives pleasure through its enjoyment and pain through its suffering; and it is established that the dead person sits up in his grave and answers the questioning of the two angels, peace be upon them both], no one among you is able to escape from that greatness (p-300) which encompasses His majestic greatness nor His subtle wisdom. ﴿And from it﴾ [not from anything else] ﴿We bring you out﴾ on the Day of Resurrection by that very same greatness ﴿once more﴾ as We began you [the first time], just as We did with plants, alike. It is known that this is the act of the One, the Chooser, not the act of natures. Once He made you living from a thing that has no origin in animality at all, and again He returned you to what you were before life: dust with no spirit in it nor anything resembling it. There is no doubt that the One who does that is capable of bringing you out from it living, just as He began that; indeed, restoration is easier in the customary course of things.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 20, verse 56:

Since what he mentioned, of the things that pertain to the earth such as the elbows and other parts, was at a degree of clarity beyond which there is no further aim, the meaning becomes: We showed Pharaoh this one whom We have mentioned to you, [together with] Our signs and others. And since the context calls for magnifying (ta'zim) the power (qudrah), He followed it with His saying: ﴿And We indeed showed him﴾, that is, with the staff and the hand and others of what has preceded, from the requirement of Our greatness, ﴿Our signs﴾ [that is, whose greatness is from Our greatness], ﴿all of them﴾ [with the eye and the heart], because whoever has power over the like of that has power over others like it of extraordinary events (khawariq al-'adat), since possible things are equal in relation to His power, especially since the one who mentioned the mother-signs (ummahat al-ayat), as he will be pointed to, God willing, in [Surat al-Anbiya'] ﴿but he denied﴾, that is, them, ﴿and refused﴾, that is, to send the Children of Israel. This is more eloquent than enumerating what was mentioned in al-A'raf. It is as if it was said: How did he act in his denial and refusal? So it was said:

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 20, verse 57:

﴿Said﴾ when he found no accusation that could stir the Copts to zeal for their own selves, since he knew the truth of what Musa had brought, its manifestness, and the acceptance of minds towards it. So he feared that the people would follow him and abandon him, and he grew extremely weak within himself, through contemplating his words, singly and in combination, knowing their worth: ﴿"Have you come to us to drive us out of our land"﴾, this land of which we are its possessors, ﴿"with your magic, O Musa?"﴾ So he made it appear to his followers that this was magic, and that, together with what they had become accustomed to of their habit in misguidance, became a deterrent for them from following the clear evidence they had seen,

Then he connected with the causal fa' (al-fa' al-sababiyyah, the "fa" of consequence) his statement, emphasized (mu'akkidan) as a notice (iadhan) of his knowledge that whatever Moses had brought, every one who sees it denies that anyone other than him could match it: ﴿So We will surely bring you﴾, meaning [by the Supreme God!], with a promise that admits no failure, ﴿sorcery like it﴾, as an affirmation of what they had imagined by it. Then he displayed fairness and justice in order to bind his people firmly, so he said: ﴿So set up between us and you an appointment﴾, meaning of time and place, ﴿which we will not fail, neither we nor you﴾, meaning we will not make it behind us, by sitting back from coming to it.

Since each of time and place cannot be separated from the other, he said: ﴿a place﴾, and he chose to mention the place for the sake of describing it by his saying: ﴿level﴾, meaning (p-302) just between us, with no hardship upon either of us in his intention greater than the other's hardship. Consider this speech, which he embellished, fashioned and adorned, by which he held his people back from happiness, and continued to lead them with the like of it until he brought them to the sea and drowned them, [then] in the torrents of the Fire he burned them. So it is incumbent upon the shrewd and perceptive person to scrutinize statements and deeds, thoughts and states, and to present them to the touchstone of the Sharia: the Book and the Sunnah. What agrees with them he adopts, and what does not, he abandons.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 20, verse 59:

Since the gathering of their festivity, which they were accustomed to, encompassed these purposes in terms of time, place and other things, he (peace be upon him) chose it for that reason, and so the report about it was resumed in His words, exalted is He: ﴿He said: Your appointment is the Day of Adornment﴾, that is, the aforementioned, ﴿the Day of Adornment﴾, meaning your festival on which you are accustomed to gather, at the place to which you are accustomed. Here he mentioned the time, although it implies the place because of the custom of gathering there, just as previously he mentioned the place because of its description as "the level (place)". ﴿And that the people be gathered﴾ [he made it passive -] because the intention is the gathering itself, not who does it, from a specific party ﴿the people﴾ [that is, enticing them, even if by force -] ﴿in the forenoon﴾, so that it meets the day from its beginning, making it more manifest for what he does and clearer, and the night will not come except after the matter has been decided, and the true has been distinguished from the false. You will be at your most complete and most at leisure, so the edge of those who spread falsehood and their partisans will be blunted, and of the arrogant who stood against the truth and their followers. The story of this clear matter will spread in every desert and settlement, and it will circulate among all the people of the tents and the cities.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 20, verse 60:

﴿Then Pharaoh withdrew﴾ from Moses, to make ready what he intended of deceit after having turned away from submitting to the command of God. ﴿Then he gathered his stratagem﴾, that is, his scheming, his ruse and his deception, which he devised against Moses by assembling those through whom deceit could be achieved, namely the sorcerers. He gathered them from every quarter. The people of Egypt were the most skilled in sorcery of all the people of the earth and the most numerous in sorcerers, and in that era they were most attentive to sorcery, most accomplished in it, and most abundant in it. ﴿Then he came﴾ to the appointed time upon which the decision had been settled, with those he had gathered of the sorcerers, the soldiers, and those among the people who followed them, along with the strong motives to come to the festival and to witness that contest, the like of which had never been.

When the listener became eager to learn what Moses (peace be upon him) did at that moment, the Exalted resumed the account of him with His saying: ﴿He said to them﴾, that is, to the people of deceit, who were the magicians and others, ﴿Moses﴾, when he saw their gathering, advising them: ﴿Woe to you﴾, O people whom God created for His worship, ﴿do not invent a lie against God﴾, that is, do not deliberately set about fabricating a falsehood against God, by making His great and established signs into mere magic having no reality, by claiming that what you conjure by illusion is real when it is not illusion, and by associating others with Him; (p-304) and from this he drew the consequence of his words: ﴿lest He destroy you﴾, that is, lest He annihilate you. Al-Razi said: its root meaning is uprooting, ﴿with a punishment﴾, that is, a mighty one by which your failure will become manifest, ﴿and indeed he fails﴾, every one ﴿who fabricates﴾, that is, who deliberately tells a lie against God or against anyone else.

﴿So they disputed their affair among themselves﴾, i.e., the magicians pulled their affair in different directions (tajadhdhaba) when they heard these words, knowing that he (Moses) could not confront Pharaoh with the like of it, with all of his soldiers and followers, and would not be safe from him [except -] one with whom God is. ﴿And they conferred in secret﴾, i.e., their speech, which they conducted in private consultation and took great care to conceal, for secret counsel (al-najwa) is concealment, lest Pharaoh and his followers should discover their disagreement [in -] which the word "dispute" (al-tanazu') implies. It is as if it was said: What did they say when their dispute came to an end? [So it was said -]:

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 20, verse 63:

﴿They said﴾, that is, the magicians, after reflection and turning the matter over in their minds: what Pharaoh had suggested to them, by way of instruction from him and seeking his favour, with what would turn people away from Musa and Harun, peace be upon them both [and discourage them from following the two of them, even if they prevail, because the defeat of one magician by another magician cannot be denied]: ﴿Indeed, these two﴾, that is, Musa and Harun. It is also read as "Hadhani" with an alif, according to the dialect of those who make the alif of the dual obligatory in every case. Abu Hayyan said: this is the dialect of several groups of the Arabs: Banu al-Harith ibn Ka'b, some of Kinanah, Khath'am, Zubayd, Banu al-'Anbar (p-305), Banu al-Hujaym, Murad and 'Udhrah.

﴿are surely two magicians﴾, there being no doubt about this on their part, ﴿who want﴾, that is, [by what] they say of the claim to prophethood and other things, ﴿to drive you out﴾, O people, ﴿from your land﴾, this one to which you have become accustomed, and which is your homeland, generation after generation, ﴿by their magic﴾, which they have displayed to you and other things.

[And since every party rejoices in what it has,] they said: ﴿and to do away with your way﴾, this magical way which you have toiled to establish, and in which your forefathers spent their lives, until its matter reached its extreme, ﴿and your religion﴾, by which your affairs are sustained, ﴿the best﴾, that is, the way which is the most excellent of ways, so that they would be more esteemed, by what they display of it, in the eyes of the people [than you], and would turn the faces of the people toward it and away from you, and what you have of provision and greatness in the eyes of the elite and the common folk would be nullified by that, along with other aims.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 20, verse 64:

﴿So gather your plot﴾, i.e., leave nothing of it behind without bringing it, and do not dispute among yourselves, lest you become weak. ﴿Then come forward﴾ to the encounter with Musa and Harun for the contest between them, ﴿in a row﴾, i.e., competing and equal in the contest, so that your affair may prevail over them and you may succeed. Lining up in rows (al-isti'faf, i.e., standing in orderly lines) is more awe-inspiring in the hearts of those who see.

Since the implied sense is: [whoever -] comes thus [has -] prevailed, he (al-Biqa'i) joined to it their statement, as a confirmation: ﴿And indeed he has succeeded today﴾ in this gathering, the like of which has never been gathered at all, ﴿who prevails﴾, i.e., overcomes and attains dominance. That is, they did what was preceded and came in a row. When they came, and they were knowledgeable enough to say what would benefit them in opposing Musa, peace be upon him, the report about him was resumed with His statement, exalted is He:

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 20, verse 65:

﴿They said﴾, that is, the magicians, calling out, "because gentle speech toward an opponent, if it does not benefit, does no harm": ﴿O Moses, either you throw﴾ what is with you, of that with which you debate us first, ﴿or we will be the first to throw﴾, that is, we ourselves, ﴿the first to throw﴾ what is with him.

Said [Moses], in response to their courtesy, "[by something better than it]"; and because he understood that their intention was to go first, and that they wanted to be the last, so that they would have the final word by subjecting his miracle to their magic, and no doubt would remain afterward: "Rather, I will not throw first; you throw first." So they seized the opportunity, because that was their intention, as they understood it from the wording of the context and the explicit mention of "first." So they threw, and "behold, their ropes and their staffs," which they had thrown, "were imagined to him" (and he is Our chosen one) "[as an imagining that began]" "from their magic," by which they had outdone the people of the earth, "that they" (because of the intensity of their agitation) "were moving" with a movement. And if this was his condition, although he was the most firm of people in sight and the most penetrating in insight, then what is your opinion of anyone else?

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 20, verse 67:

﴿Fa-awjasa﴾ means he concealed (aḍmara) within himself because of that. Its literal sense is: he caused a wājis to arise, that is, a passing thought (khāṭir) and an inward impulse (ḍamīr).

Since the setting is one of displaying extraordinary signs through his hands, it might have been understood that he caused this fear to arise in the soul of someone other than himself. Therefore the setting calls for emphasis by placing the complement first, and he said accordingly—not for the sake of observing the rhyme-endings (fawāṣil)—﴿fī nafsihi﴾, meaning within himself specifically. [He placed first what the setting is for and what it emphasizes, and so said:] ﴿khīfatan Mūsā﴾, like the fear he felt of his staff when he first saw it moving, in this way, according to the natural disposition of human beings. And in view of the natural disposition, he expressed it with "soul" (nafs) rather than, for example, "heart" (qalb).

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 20, verse 68:

When that had come about, and it was known that Allah was with him, and that He was worthy [of -] nullifying their magic, He resumed the report about him with His words: ﴿We said﴾ [by what We have of greatness -]: ﴿Do not fear﴾ of anything from their affair or otherwise. Then He gave the reason for that in His words, and emphasized it with kinds of emphasis, because the situation required [the denial that anyone should overcome what they displayed of their magic, given its magnitude]: ﴿Indeed, you are the one who is supreme﴾ [i.e., specifically -] ﴿the supreme﴾, meaning the one who prevails with a manifest victory about which there is no doubt.

﴿And cast﴾. He pointed to the right-hand side (yumn) of the staff and its blessing by His saying: ﴿what is in your right hand﴾, meaning: from this staff which We told you about when We first honored you with conversation (munājāt), ﴿And what is that in your right hand, O Musa?﴾ [Ta-Ha: 17]. Then We showed you of it what We showed you. ﴿It will swallow﴾ with strength and effort, with a speed that can hardly be perceived, as indicated by the omission of the letter tā' (in the verb). ﴿What they have made﴾ [i.e., what they did after great training in it (p-308) and long practice].

Then he gave the reason for that in His saying: ﴿Indeed, what﴾ [i.e., that which] ﴿they have made﴾, i.e., [that] their making [is something] ﴿you have seen, and whose affair has alarmed you﴾.

Since the aim was to belittle this host, he used the singular and the indefinite, because the genitive (muḍāf) is indefinite and belittled, so He said: ﴿a sorcerer's trick﴾, i.e., a magical trick with no reality and no permanence, [whether it is one person or many. Had he used the plural, it would have been imagined that the intended point was the number. And since the sense was -]: ﴿they do not prosper﴾. He followed it with His saying: ﴿and the sorcerer does not prosper, wherever he comes﴾, i.e., this kind [of person], ﴿wherever he comes﴾, i.e., however he proceeds and by whatever way he takes, for he only does what has no reality. So [Musa] complied with what his Lord commanded him, namely casting his staff, and what He had promised him of its swallowing what they had made came to pass without the staff showing any increase in thickness or anything else, even though their ropes and staffs were a great many things. Thus everyone who saw that knew its truth and the falsity of what the sorcerers did. The sorcerers from among them hastened to submit to the command of God, prostrating themselves with the haste of one who had been thrown down upon his face. For this reason, after mentioning their trickery and their effort in opposing Musa, peace be upon him, [and -] He omitted mention of the casting and what caused it of the (p-309) swallowing, because the aim of the surah is the power to soften hard hearts.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 20, verse 70:

﴿So the magicians were thrown down﴾, meaning: what they saw of God's command overcame them with the greatest speed and with the easiest of matters, ﴿prostrating﴾ on their faces. Al-Isfahani said: "Glory be to God! How great is their station! They threw down their ropes and their staffs in disbelief and denial, then they threw down their heads after an hour in gratitude and prostration. How great is the difference between the two throwings!" It is as if someone said: "This was their action, so what did they say?" It was said: ﴿They said: "We believe"﴾, meaning: "We affirmed."

Since the context of this surah required placing Harun (peace be upon him) first, He said: ﴿by the Lord of Harun and Musa﴾. This is good news to the Prophet (ﷺ) that He, glorified is He, will not make him wretched through this Qur'an, but will guide people through it [bihi] and make them submissive to it. He will make the Arabs, despite their haughtiness, the most humble of people toward His ministers, helpers and successors, even though they are the weakest of people and their tribes the least of tribes. This also shows the sincerity of their faith and the purity of their claim, by placing the translating minister first, ascending gradually in the ranks of knowledge, from the one who conveyed this to them, to the one who commanded him with it, and then to the one who sent him, thanking the benefactors in sequence: "He who does not give thanks to people does not give thanks to God." This [order] is for what required placing him first here, not for this alone.

They also mentioned the name of the Lord as an indication that He, glorified is He, showed kindness to both of them by elevating their status above the magicians, and above those who used to acknowledge lordship, namely Pharaoh, who did not avail them anything. Thus they were magicians at the beginning of the day and righteous martyrs at its end. This verse, and similar verses in this surah (p. 310) and elsewhere, in which something is placed first though it would seem that its proper place is later, and vice versa, are due to subtle aspects of meaning. These are what led some who were not firmly grounded to say that the Qur'an observes the fawasil (verse endings) just as the eloquent Arabs contrive saj' (rhymed prose), and a group of later scholars followed him by imitation. The Prophet (ﷺ) criticized this when he said: "Rhymed prose like the rhymed prose of the Jahiliyyah, or he said: of the soothsayers."

It is known from what I have mentioned that the meaning upon which this surah is built could not be ordered except by placing Harun first. This is supported by the fact that here He said ﴿Indeed, we are a messenger﴾ [Ta-Ha: 47], while in al-Shu'ara' it is "messenger" (singular). Imam Fakhr al-Din al-Razi said, as Shaykh Abu Hayyan reported from him in [the surah of Fatir] in al-Nahr: "It is not said regarding any part of the Qur'an that it was placed first or last for the sake of saj', because the miraculous nature of the Qur'an does not lie in mere wording, but in both wording and meaning." [And] Qadi Abu Bakr al-Baqillani said in his book I'jaz al-Qur'an: "All our companions have held that there is no saj' in the Qur'an." Abu al-Hasan al-Ash'ari also mentioned this in more than one place in his books. Then he refuted the opponent by saying: "What they suppose to be saj' is a mistake, because a statement may be in the pattern of saj' without being saj', since saj' follows the wording, in which the meaning is subordinate to the words that produce the saj'. This is not the case with what coincidentally occurs in the Qur'an in the manner of saj', because there the wording comes subordinate to the meaning. There is a distinction between a statement being ordered in itself through its words, which convey the intended meaning, and a meaning being ordered without the wording. When meaning is bound to saj', the benefit of the saj' is like the benefit of anything else. When meaning is ordered by itself without saj', the saj' is used only to embellish the speech and not to correct the meaning." He then supported this with noble proofs, expanding on them and excelling in doing so, may God have mercy on him. What greatly benefits this matter has already been mentioned at the end of [the surah of al-Tawbah].

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 20, verse 71:

Since Musa (peace be upon him) was the one intended by the sending [to Pharaoh], Allah the Exalted resumed the report about Pharaoh at the time when that [matter] reached him, so He said: [Pharaoh] said — that is, Pharaoh said to the magicians, rebuking them — [and He concealed his name here and did not disclose it as He did in al-A'raf, because the aim of the surah is gentleness toward those who are called and forbearance toward them, and he is not worthy of having his name mentioned in this station]: ﴿You believed in him﴾, that is, in Allah, ﴿before I gave you permission﴾, that is, you believed in Him or followed Musa, ﴿before I gave you permission﴾ to do so, [giving the impression] that he would give permission [for it], so that the people would hold back from hastening to follow, caught between fear of punishment and hope of permission. Then he resumed his speech, giving a reason and casting doubt upon his followers in order to turn them away from following [the magicians]: ﴿Indeed, he is your chief﴾, that is, in knowledge, ﴿who taught you magic﴾. So you did not follow him because the truth had become manifest; rather, out of your desire for some of the deceit, you agreed with him on it before your presence (p-312) at this place. This is in keeping with his habit of casting doubt upon his followers regarding whatever keeps them from following the truth.

When he had cast doubt upon them, he began to increase their confusion by threatening the magicians, so he said: ﴿Then I will surely cut off﴾, that is, because of what you did, ﴿your hands﴾ in a distributive manner ﴿and your feet﴾, that is, from each one a hand and a foot, ﴿on opposite sides﴾. So when I cut off the right hand, I will cut off the left foot. ﴿And I will surely crucify you﴾ [and he expressed elevation by the term of place, indicating that he would give them power over the one crucified in it, the way a contained thing is held within its container, so he said]: ﴿on the trunks of date palms﴾, as a means of making your killing abhorrent, to deter the likes of you. ﴿And you will surely know which of us﴾, I or the Lord of Musa, who said that the punishment is upon whoever denies and turns away, ﴿has a severer and more lasting punishment﴾, that is, in terms of punishment, meaning which of us has the more severe punishment and the longer duration.

When they realized what he had cast upon the minds of the weak, they warned them. So God Exalted informed about that by His saying, resuming: ﴿They said, "We will never prefer you"﴾, meaning we will not put your trace first by following you, so that we may be safe from your passing punishment, ﴿over the clear proofs that have come to us﴾ through Moses, peace be upon him, which we witnessed and knew that no one can match. When they began with what points to the Creator through the extraordinary act, they ascended to mentioning Him after knowing Him through His act, indicating His exalted rank. So they said: (p-٣١٣)﴿and He who created us﴾, meaning, nor will we prefer you by following you over Him who originated our creation. This indicates that His lordship (rububiyyah) extends over them, over Him, and over all people, and it alerts to Pharaoh's inability before the One who truly deserves worship. In all these statements of theirs there is a great exaltation of God Exalted in expression and allusion, and a great belittling of Pharaoh.

When this resulted in their not caring about him, knowing that what he did was by God's permission, they said: ﴿So decree what﴾, meaning do in your judgment what ﴿you decree﴾. Then they gave the reason for that in their saying: ﴿You can only decree﴾, meaning you can only do with us what you wish if God empowers you over it, ﴿this worldly life﴾, meaning your judgment during its duration falls only upon the body. So it is an hour that is followed by rest. We fear none but the One who judges over the soul even if the body perishes, and that is the One of severe punishment, the enduring Recompense with reward or punishment. [Perhaps they dropped the preposition out of concession, that even if his judgment were supposed to extend to the end of the world, he would be worthy of not being feared, because it is perishing, and God's punishment is lasting.]

Then they gave a reason for this sealing by their words: ﴿Indeed, whoever comes to his Lord as a criminal, for him is Hell; he will neither die therein nor live.﴾ "His Lord" means the One who nurtured him and bestowed His favor upon him, by bringing him into existence and providing for him everything that would make him right. "Criminal" means one who cuts off what He commanded to be joined. "Hell" is the abode of humiliation, ﴿wherein he will neither die﴾ ever, despite the severity of its punishment.

Unlike your punishment, which, [if -] it became severe, would cause death, and so it would pass quickly. If it were light, it would not be lasting, and its end would be death, however long it lasted. ﴿Nor will he live﴾ therein a life from which he could benefit.

﴿And whoever comes to Him﴾, that is, to his Lord who brought him into being and nurtured him, ﴿as a believer﴾, that is, one who affirms Him.

[Since he had earlier stated that mere disbelief necessitates punishment, this was a place where one would expect a statement about the belief of the one who believes in the same way, so he said -]: "qad" [meaning -] he added to that, confirming his faith, that he ﴿did﴾, that is, in this world, ﴿righteous deeds﴾ which he was commanded to perform, [so it is as if - true -] faith necessitates righteous deeds. ﴿Then those﴾, that is, those of high rank, ﴿for them﴾ [that is, because their essences naturally call them to this by the demand of their innate disposition] ﴿are the high ranks﴾, which have no comparison to the ranks You promised us.

Then they clarified it by their saying: ﴿Gardens of Eden﴾, meaning they were prepared for abiding, and its causes were arranged within them, ﴿beneath which rivers flow﴾, meaning beneath their chambers, their couches and their land; so no spot in them is desired for a river to flow through without it flowing. Then by His saying ﴿abiding therein﴾ He made clear that its people were likewise prepared for lasting residence.

And since the context, and the conjunction with a not-apparent antecedent [and -], guided to the meaning that the estimate is: that great recompense and enduring bliss is the recompense of those described (as such), because of their purifying themselves, He followed it with His saying: ﴿And that is the recompense of﴾ everyone who ﴿purifies himself﴾, meaning who cleanses his self by what has been mentioned of faith and righteous deeds. In this there is consolation for the Companions, may Allah be pleased with them, regarding what was being done to them at the revelation of (p-316) this surah, when they were oppressed.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (*Nazm al-Durar*) on surah 20, verse 77:

When Allah, glory be to Him, had explained the arrogance of Pharaoh that was claimed in His saying ﴿But he denied and refused﴾ [Ta-Ha: 56], and concluded it by saying that He destroys the disobedient, whoever they may be, and saves the obedient, He followed that with a tangible witness to it, one that shows that nothing of Pharaoh's power or arrogance availed him. So He said, conjoining it to ﴿And We had indeed shown him Our signs﴾ [Ta-Ha: 56], ﴿And We had indeed revealed﴾, that is, by Our greatness, to facilitate what comes after of great affairs, ﴿to Musa﴾, being unconcerned with anything of Pharaoh's words or deeds. This revelation came a long time after the matter of the magicians, during which lengthy calamities occurred, through which the great signs took place. It is as though these were omitted because of what they indicate of the hardness of hearts. The purpose here is the conclusion of what preceded of the surah's intended meaning. ﴿Travel by night﴾, that is, at night, because *al-Surā* is the travelling of the night. He honoured them by attributing them to Himself, so He said: ﴿with My servants﴾, that is, the Children of Israel, whom He had turned Pharaoh's heart toward, until he permitted their departure after having refused to release them or to cease punishing them. So head with them toward the direction of the Sea of al-Qulzum. ﴿And strike for them﴾, that is, act by striking the sea with your staff; for this reason it is called a striking.

Since striking the sea with the staff was the cause of the existence of the described path, He attributed the act to it, so He said: ﴿a path in the sea﴾, and described it with the verbal noun [for emphasis], so He said: ﴿dry﴾, while it is [or you are] ﴿not fearing﴾, and by this is meant the genus, for each tribe had a path. ﴿Overtaken﴾, that is, that something of the sea's surge or the enemy's violence should overtake you [or other than that].

Since overtaking is shared between catching up and pursuit, He followed it with His saying: ﴿and not fearing﴾, that is, fearing nothing else at all, in carrying out My command and rescuing those whom I sent you to rescue. Presenting it in this manner, with the display of power and the belittling of the obstinate one despite his pride and his authority, is an observed demonstration of what He established at the beginning of the surah concerning the comprehensiveness of power and the encompassing of knowledge, as good tidings that this religion will prevail through the multitude of followers, the destruction of opponents, the happiness of turning enemies back, and the transformation of their hatred into affection, even if they are a stubborn people.

Then He followed this with His saying [by way of coordination with an implied sense: so they hastened to carry out the command concerning the night journey and other matters]: ﴿So Pharaoh followed them﴾, that is, [he caused pursuit and marching behind] the Children of Israel despite their humiliation and weakness, ﴿Pharaoh with his hosts﴾ despite their numbers, their strength, their loftiness and their might. Thus they were like a follower that has no meaning without its leader. ﴿Then there covered them﴾, that is, Pharaoh and his people, ﴿of the sea﴾, that is, the sea [which by its nature is to be deep and overwhelming; he was brief and yet awe-inspiring, and said]: ﴿that which covered them﴾, that is, a matter whose true description the minds cannot bear to convey, so He destroyed their first and last, and cut off their root, leaving none of them alive. And no thorn pricked any of Our servants who were oppressed.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 20, verse 79:

﴿And Pharaoh misled﴾ his people, despite his cunning, ﴿his people﴾, along with the strength of their bodies and its meanings.

Since affirming the act does not convey generality, he negated its opposite in order to convey it, and this is more emphatic, more striking to the soul, and more awe-inspiring to it. So he said: ﴿And he did not guide﴾, meaning that no part of guidance proceeded from him, neither for himself nor for anyone among his people. Thus the evident proof was complete, demonstrating the complete power to deliver the obedient and destroy the disobedient.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 20, verse 80:

When this was bound to arouse eagerness to know what happened to the Children of Israel after it, God the Exalted said, healing this thirst (for knowledge): We turned to the Children of Israel, bestowing favor upon them by what has passed and what is yet to come, saying: ﴿O Children of Israel﴾, acknowledging to them that We looked at the earlier deeds and so honored them (p-319) for the sake of their father.

Since repelling harms and removing obstacles come before bringing benefits and securing advantages, He said: ﴿We have certainly delivered you﴾ by Our overwhelming power ﴿from your enemy﴾, the one before whom you were the most contemptible of things.

When they were free to carry out what was required of them of obedience, He said: ﴿And We made an appointment with you﴾, that is, all of you, as has passed in al-Baqarah from the text of the Torah, for presenting yourselves in Our presence and taking pride in the places of Our mercy ﴿at the right side of the Mount﴾, that is, the side on your right hand as you face this direction in which your faces are turned toward the House of [your father -] Ibrahim, peace be upon him, [and it is its side which adjoins the sea, and the region of Makkah and Yemen -].

Having begun with the religious benefit, he followed it with the worldly benefit, [so he said -]: ﴿And We sent down upon you﴾, after the sending down of this Book in this appointment, to revive your spirits, ﴿the manna and the quail﴾, to sustain your bodies. Thus he began with the deliverance that enables worship, then followed it with the blessing of the Book that guides to it, then with the strengthening provision, and he indicated [the blessing of -] permission regarding it by His saying:

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 20, verse 81:

﴿Eat﴾ indicates its abundance by His saying: ﴿of the good things that﴾, and indicates its greatness by His saying: ﴿We have provided you﴾, from that and from other than that.

Since wealth and ease are the cause of generosity, He said: ﴿and do not transgress therein﴾ (p-320) by storing it up for tomorrow on other than Friday, nor by any other form of wantonness and neglect of gratitude, by spending it on other than obedience, ﴿lest there descend upon you﴾, that is, lest there come down [and become obligatory at its time, which is the most fitting time for it], according to the reading of the majority with the kasra (fa-yahilla), and a great descending and a severe falling, according to the reading of al-Kisa'i with the damma (fa-yuhalla), ﴿My wrath upon you﴾, so that you perish thereby. And the reading "wa" ("and") every one ("kull") "upon whom My wrath descends" ("man yuhallilu 'alayhi ghadabi") among you and among others. ﴿Then he has fallen﴾, that is, his state became that of one who has fallen from a height.

When man is the seat of error however hard he strives, He gives him hope and wins his favour by saying: ﴿And indeed I am Forgiving (Ghaffar) to whoever repents﴾, meaning, the Concealer who lets the hem of pardon fall over sins, ﴿to whoever repents﴾, meaning, turns back from his sins, from polytheism and what is close to it, ﴿and believes﴾ in everything that belief in it is obligatory, ﴿and does righteous deeds﴾ confirming his faith.

Since the rank of persisting in uprightness is at the highest level, He expressed it with the particle of delay (thumma, "then"), saying: ﴿then is guided﴾, meaning, he persists in righteous deeds, earnestly seeking to perform them according to Our command and in the most pleasing manner to Us, with utmost turning towards that, as indicated by the form ifta'ala (the eighth verbal form, which denotes effort and exertion). It seems that when God, glorified is He, arranged the stations of the people of Musa (Moses), peace be upon him, in general and of the seventy chosen men in particular on the mountain, as has passed from the text of the Tawrat (Torah) in Surat al-Baqarah, and promised him speech after thirty nights without specifying its first night for him, it seems that, out of longing for what he had seen of being made known to Him through the station of beauty (maqam al-jamal), he did not wait for a specific permission from God, exalted is He, at the first time of coming, being content with the general command given earlier regarding the appointment. So he hastened ten days ahead of the time that God knew the speech would occur after the thirty He had set for that. Musa, peace be upon him, commanded his people [at -] his rising, and instructed them to follow him and to remain in his footsteps, to settle in the places God had assigned for them, and he commanded the chosen seventy likewise. It seems that when he departed, they lingered because of what they had seen of the station of majesty (maqam al-jalal). When the thirty days passed after Musa's departure, the time God wished for the conversation had not yet come, so He added ten more. The Children of Israel then entertained suspicions during those ten, and what happened of taking the calf befell them.

Now when that happened (and God knows best what happened), and when the greatest of what had passed in the verse of favour upon them and the making known of blessings to them was the promise to guide them through visible and audible signs, and He concluded that with an indication to striving in turning towards guidance, He followed that with mention of their going astray after seeing what is far, in every respect, from being led astray by anything at all, all of this to show complete power to control hearts in the opposite of what is supposed of them. The fulfilment of promises is the most delicious thing to hearts and the most desirable to souls. The context was necessarily guiding to (p-322) the estimation: "They came to the Mount and made for its right side by Our command and Our will, and Moses, Our chosen one, hastened the ascent to it, [hurrying towards what he had of longing for that noble station, and the coming of his people was delayed from coming along with him, so We said: What has delayed your people from coming with you?] Then He joined to it His words: ﴿And what has hastened you away from your people﴾, i.e., what thing made you hasten in coming ﴿away from your people﴾, even though you had hastened with the haste of one who goes to great lengths to seek contentment, [did you not know that the bounds of kings should not be exceeded by going ahead or lagging behind?] ﴿O Moses﴾. So why did you not come all together and wait for a new command concerning the time at which I summon you?

﴿He said﴾ Moses, thinking that they had hurried ahead of him: ﴿They are [the ones] behind me﴾ [He used the demonstrative and dropped from it the *ha' al-tanbih* (the particle of alerting), because it is not fitting in addressing God. Ibn Hubayra said: "I have not seen any of the chosen ones (*al-asfiya'*) address his Lord with that. He addressed the disbelievers with it, because of their dullness."

﴿They will say, "Our Lord, these are our partners whom we used to call upon besides You"﴾ [an-Nahl 16:86], in its like. As for the end of az-Zukhruf, he has mentioned the use of it in its place.] ﴿These [are]﴾, meaning they are so near that one can travel to them, being ﴿upon my trail﴾, meaning walking in the traces of my walk before it was effaced. I did not outstrip them except by something that customarily happens in outstripping [of this kind] ﹰ among companions. This was his building upon what he had agreed with them and what he had emphatically enjoined upon them. Then he made excuse for his action, saying: ﴿And I hastened﴾, (p-323) I myself, by hastening ﴿to You﴾, and he followed the custom of those near [to God] as is their right, so he said: ﴿My Lord﴾, meaning O You who hasten in setting right my affair and in bringing good to me, ﴿that You may be pleased﴾ with me with a pleasure greater than what was before.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 20, verse 85:

﴿Said﴾ the Lord, glorified is He: ﴿Indeed, We﴾, meaning [certainly -] as a consequence of your haste regarding them, ﴿have tested﴾, meaning We mixed with your people through Our greatness in a mixing that inclined and altered them, ﴿your people﴾ by your hastening.

Since the trial did not encompass the whole of the time that came after him, but was only in part of it, He introduced the preposition and said: ﴿after you﴾ [meaning We mixed with them through a matter of Our affairs, a mixing that transformed them from what you had known them to be -], and this was after the completion of the period you had set for them, which was thirty [nights], in actuality and in potential only, from the first moment you departed from them [by your setting of that period -] [considering that your first coming -] was the very thing that caused the trial, by increasing the days of absence on account of it, because We added to the end of the period an amount equal to what you hastened in its beginning. When your return to them was delayed, the trials actually befell them, and so they assumed conjectures that were prone to stoning.

When the trial enveloped them all except twelve thousand out of more than six hundred thousand, (p-324) He attributed misguidance to all of them, saying: ﴿and the Samiri misled them﴾, meaning away from the path of right guidance, by what he caused for them. Al-Nasa'i related in his Tafsir within his Sunan, and Abu Ya'la in his Musnad, and Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim in their two tafsirs, from Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with him and his father, in the hadith of the trial, that when Musa, peace be upon him, was promised by his Lord that He would speak to him, he appointed his brother Harun, peace be upon him, as successor over his people, and set for them a term of thirty days. He went and fasted them, its nights and its days. Then he disliked to speak to his Lord while the smell of his mouth had changed, so he chewed some plant of the earth. His Lord said to him: "Do you not know that the smell of the fasting person is better with Me than the smell of musk? Return and fast ten more." When the people of Musa saw that he had not returned to them, that grieved them. Harun had addressed them and said: "You left Egypt, and the people of Pharaoh have with you borrowed goods and deposits, and for you there is the like of them. I think you should count what you have with them. I do not permit you a deposit entrusted to you, nor a loan, and we shall not return any of that to them, nor keep it for ourselves." So he dug a pit and commanded each people who had with them any of those goods, or ornaments, to cast them into that pit. Then he kindled the fire and burned it, (p-325) and said: "It shall belong neither to us nor to them." The Samiri was from a people who worshipped cows, neighbours of the Children of Israel, but he was not of the Children of Israel. He went out with Musa and the Children of Israel when they set out. Then it was decreed for him that he saw a trace, so he grasped [a handful -] from it. He passed by Harun, and Harun, peace be upon him, said to him: "O Samiri! Will you not throw down what is in your hand?" - and he was holding it, and no one saw it throughout that day. He said: "This is a handful from the trace of the Messenger who brought you across the sea, [and -] I will not throw it down for anything, unless you pray to Allah that, when I throw it, what I want will come to be." So he threw it, and Harun prayed for him. He said: "I want it to be a calf." So what was in the pit of goods, ornaments, brass or iron, gathered together and became a hollow calf with no spirit in it, having a lowing sound. Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with him and his father, said: "No, by Allah! It never had any sound at all; rather, the wind would enter through its rear and exit through its mouth, and that sound was from that." The Children of Israel then split into factions. One faction said: "O Samiri! What is this, and you know best about it?" He said: "This is your Lord, but Musa has lost the way." One faction said: "We will not deny this until Musa returns to us. If it is our Lord, we did not neglect Him and fail regarding Him when we saw Him; and if it is not our Lord, we will follow Musa." And one faction said: "This is the work of Satan, and it is not our Lord, and we will not believe in it nor affirm it." (p-326) And another faction had the truth of what the Samiri said about the calf instilled in their hearts, and they openly denied it - the hadith.

Then he explained, by God's informing him of that, His saying: ﴿So Musa returned﴾ to his people, i.e., when his Lord informed him of that, ﴿to his people﴾, meaning those who had great strength over what they attempted, ﴿angry and grieved﴾, meaning greatly sorrowful or angry. [And he resumed his speech]: ﴿He said﴾ to his people when he returned to them, seeking their goodwill: ﴿O my people﴾. He rebuked them with his saying: ﴿Did not your Lord promise you﴾, whose kindness to you has been long, ﴿a good promise﴾, i.e., that He would send down to you a protecting Book, expiate your sins, and give you victory over your enemies, and other of His honours.

Since it is customary that the passage of time undermines resolutions and alters covenants, as Abu al-'Ala' Ahmad ibn Sulayman al-Ma'arri said in this verse:

*Whenever long time passes between us, I will not forget you, for many a beloved whose covenant has lengthened has been forgotten.*

Since he, peace be upon him, was close in time to them, he denied the long lapse by saying, resuming [from what its implied sense is: Has your Lord abandoned His promises to you and cut off His bounty from you?]: ﴿Has the time seemed long to you?﴾, i.e., [the period of] His kindness to you, so that you changed from what I left you upon, as those of base vices are subject to the loosening of resolve due to weakness of intellect and little reflection. ﴿Or did you desire﴾ by breaking [it], despite the nearness of the covenant and the mention of the pact, ﴿that wrath from your Lord should descend upon you﴾, i.e., from the Benefactor to you, due to worshipping the calf? Neither matter occurred. The first is obvious; as for the second, no one is thought to intend it. The gist is that he says: you did what no sensible person would do. ﴿So you broke my promise﴾, i.e., as a consequence of your action you broke ﴿my appointment﴾ in honouring God and coming to the place He set for you, for His speaking to me and sending down His Book upon me, a kindness to you and an approach to you. It seems he attributed the appointment to himself out of courtesy toward God and to magnify Him. Alternatively, since breaking a firm, specified appointment, with no doubt about it, given the clear proofs set up and the evident demonstrations, could only be due to forgetfulness from the long time or stubborn obstinacy from bad intent, and since the most eloquent aim and clearest establishment is to compel the opponent through questioning into admitting the intended meaning, he asked them about determining one of the two matters, although a prolonged time cannot be claimed. So he said, meaning: has the time been long for you by an addition of ten days, so that you forgot, and there was no blame on you for breaking it? Or did you want wrath to descend upon you, so that you were obstinate?

So the verse is of *ihtibak* (a rhetorical device, lit. "knotting," in which two contrasting items are mentioned and each one's counterpart is omitted, relying on the other). Mention of the long time that necessitates forgetting, first, indicates the omission of obstinacy, second. And mention of wrath descending, second, indicates the negation of blame, first. The secret of that is that mentioning the cause, which is the long time, is more indicative of forgetting, which is the effect. And affirming the wrath, which is the effect, is more painful than affirming its cause, which is obstinacy.

When the listener became eager to hear their answer, the text resumed by mentioning it, saying: ﴿They said﴾: [There was none of that. -]

Since the purpose of this whole context is to show the great power of God, He expressed it with His words, relating what they said in acknowledgment of what Moses, peace be upon him, had established against them concerning their obstinacy, while offering an excuse by means of power. Yet such an excuse does not avert the punishment due for the sin: ﴿We did not break our promise to you by our own power﴾. That is: "You have indeed spoken truly in what you said, but we did not do that while we were in control of our affairs." This is according to the reading of the majority (al-jama'ah) with a kasra. According to the reading of Nafi' and 'Asim with a fatha, the meaning is: "We have a capacity by which we act upon ourselves." According to the reading of Hamzah and al-Kisa'i with a damma, it is as if they said: "We have a dominant authority over our affairs." Moreover, they have mentioned that the three readings (qira'at, recognized variant recitations of the Qur'an) are dialects for one meaning. In al-Qamus (the dictionary of al-Fayruzabadi) it says: "Malaka yamlikuhu milkan" (with the three vowel forms): he possessed it, being able to act freely with it.

The meaning is that the Samiri adorned that for them, and Satan whispered it to them, so they did not perceive until they had followed him, [being -] as if they were led to him by chains. It has also been said that this is the speech of those who did not worship it. They excused themselves by saying that they were few and had no power to resist those who worshipped it. All of this points to the fact that God, exalted is He, is the One who directs hearts, and He is capable of turning back the unbelievers of Quraysh and the Arabs after their obstinacy, their stubbornness and their corruption.

﴿But we﴾ were ﴿burdened with loads﴾, that is, burdens of the two precious metals (gold and silver), which are the causes of sins. As was mentioned earlier in al-A'raf, God commanded them in the Torah to borrow them from the Copts, and then they betrayed them with them. It seems that this was not treachery under that law, or that God, exalted is He, permitted them to do so only with respect to the Copts. ﴿Of the ornaments of the people﴾, those whom we did not know to be any people other than them, and others are not truly deserving of this term applied to them, namely the Copts. So He decreed for us that we should cast them into the fire. The motives for this grew strong and intensified to the point that we could not restrain ourselves. ﴿So we cast them, and thus﴾, that is, then this followed a similar casting, ﴿the Samiri cast﴾, and he was a close associate who joined them from the Copts of Egypt. He cast what was with him, either of the wealth or of the trace of the Messenger, as has passed and will come. It seems that his casting was the last.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 20, verse 88:

Since the emergence of the statue came immediately after its being cast, it was as though the calf were made to be the cause of that, and so it is said, with a shift away from the first-person mode of speech as a expression of disgust at attributing the matter of the calf to the speaker: ﴿So he brought out for them﴾ [i.e., for those who drank it and worshipped it], and the placing of the pronoun in the third person supports the view of those who hold that this is the speech of someone who did not worship the calf. According to those who take it as the speech of the worshippers, the meaning is that by this they were indicating their disavowal of it and their revulsion toward it.

Since it bore a strong resemblance to calves, it is said: ﴿a calf﴾, and He placed His words ﴿a body﴾ first, so that we would know that its being a calf was a matter of form, not of substance, before His words ﴿that lowed﴾, lest it occur to the mind that it was alive, whereupon a flicker of belief in the falsehood would pass over it. ﴿Then they said﴾, i.e., as a consequence of that, the Samiri said, and whoever hastened into the trial first upon seeing it followed him in this: ﴿This﴾, pointing to the calf, which is in the form of [what it is -] (p-331) an example of foolishness, ﴿is your god and the god of Moses﴾. ﴿But he forgot﴾, i.e., as a consequence [of that] that your god, Moses forgot - by his departing from this place - his location, so he went seeking it in another place, or he forgot to mention it to you.

Since this was a cause for rebuke against whoever said this, He said: ﴿Do they not see﴾ — that is, did they say that? So their saying was caused by their blindness to the fact that ﴿it does not return a word to them﴾ — that is, that it does not reply to them with speech — and a god would not be mute. ﴿And it does not control for them any harm﴾, so that they would fear it as they feared Pharaoh, and so say that out of fear of its harm, ﴿nor any benefit﴾, so that they would say that out of hope in it.

**Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on Surah 20, verse 90:**

Since sin committed with knowledge is more hideous, and misguidance after clarification is more shameful, He said, connecting it to His words ﴿He said, "O my people, did not your Lord make you a fair promise?"﴾ [Ta-Ha: 86], or to His words ﴿They said, "We did not break our promise to you"﴾ [Ta-Ha: 87]: ﴿And Harun had already said to them﴾, meaning: even though those who did not worship it had no power to turn back those who worshipped it.

Since their statement occurred during part of that period, He said ﴿before this﴾, meaning before Musa's return, seeking to win their hearts: ﴿O my people﴾. Then he confined their affair so that their thought and their consideration would be gathered, (p. 332) [and their attention] and said: ﴿You are only being tested through it﴾, meaning [the test befell you], so you were tested regarding the soundness of your faith, your sincerity in it, and your steadfastness upon it. ﴿Through it﴾ means through this image, in bringing it forth for you in this extraordinary form that breaks the normal course of things. He emphasized it because of their denial, and said: ﴿And indeed your Lord﴾, meaning the One who brought you out of non-existence and nurtured you with kindness, ﴿is the Most Merciful﴾, alone, whose bounty is general and whose blessings are comprehensive. There is no blessing upon the righteous or the wicked except that it is from Him before the calf existed, and it remains so after it. From His mercy is the acceptance of repentance, so fear the removal of His blessings through disobedience, and hope for their abundance through obedience. ﴿So follow me﴾ with the utmost of your effort in returning to Him, ﴿and obey my command﴾ in the continuation of honor through humility before Him, and the continuation of turning toward Him. It will repel from you its harm and pour upon you its good.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 20, verse 91:

Since this was the place where one would ask what their answer was to this clear matter, about which there is no doubt, it is said: ﴿They said﴾ with harshness and obstinacy: ﴿We will not cease to be devoted to it﴾, that is, to this calf, ﴿devoted﴾, that is, remaining, gathered around it, assembled, even if we must fight over that, ﴿until Moses returns to us﴾. So he (Harun) repelled them, (p-333) and they intended to harm him, and most of them had gone astray, so he had no one with him who could strengthen him. He feared that if he fought the unbelievers with them, that would achieve nothing, and that he would kill some of them, and others of their close kin would then defend them, so that there would arise among the Children of Israel a division whose scattered parts would be hard to gather and whose multitude would be hard to restore. They had delayed returning until the return of Moses, peace be upon him, even though he had not commanded him to fight those who had gone astray. He had only said to him, ﴿And set things right, and do not follow the way of the corrupters﴾ [al-A'raf: 142]. So he saw that the right course of reform was to separate himself from them until he (Moses) came.

When he mentioned what Harun (peace be upon him) had said, [the soul turned to know what Musa (peace be upon him) said to him -] because he was his successor over them, while being a leader in his own right. So he dismissed this distress with his saying, omitting [the taking of - ] his brother by the head, because of what had preceded of mentioning it and what comes here by way of indication of it. And there was no necessity for it in this surah, one of whose greatest purposes is indicating the softening of hearts: ﴿He said﴾, i.e., Musa: ﴿O Harun﴾, you are the Prophet of Allah, my brother, my minister, and my successor. So you are the most fitting of people to be blamed by me, and the most deserving of me to reproach him. ﴿What prevented you, when﴾, i.e., at the time when, ﴿you saw them going astray﴾ from the path of guidance, and following the way of ruin, ﴿from following me in my conduct among them, by taking hold of the hand of the wrongdoer, willingly or unwillingly,﴾ (p-334) following without deviating in it from what I laid down for you in any way, by even a little deviation. He expressed this emphasis by the addition of "lā" (not) in His saying:

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 20, verse 93:

﴿Why do you not follow me?﴾ As has been mentioned more than once, when a negative particle is added to speech, it negates the opposite of its content, so it affirms the content and negates its opposite, and this is at the utmost level of emphasis. ﴿Have you then disobeyed my command?﴾ That is, have you become arrogant against following me, and as a result of that you disobeyed ﴿my command﴾. And he (Musa) seized him by his beard and head, dragging him towards himself, out of anger for the sake of Allah, the Exalted. So it is as if it was said: what did he say to him? Then it was said:

Said [Harun], answering him, appealing to his sympathy by mentioning the first homeland that joined them after the breathing of the spirit, together with the tenderness and compassion he had: "O son of my mother" — he reminded him of her specifically, even though he was his full brother, because what troubles him troubles her, and she is more tender than the father. "Do not seize me by my beard, nor by my head," i.e., by his hair. Then he gave the reason for that with his saying: "Indeed I feared that you would say," if I were harsh with them until the matter reached fighting, "You have caused division among the Children of Israel" by this action of yours, which accomplished nothing because of the small number of those who were with you and your weakness against turning them back, "and you did not observe my word" [Qur'an 20:94]. "Take my place among my people, set things right, and do not follow the way of the corrupters" [Qur'an 7:142]. He did not say, "Bring them back," even if the matter led to the sword. This is like the Prophet (ﷺ) being commanded to pardon, to forbear, and to repel with gentleness when the helper is weak and the supporters are few. (p-335)

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 20, verse 95:

When he had finished advising the one closest to him, the most deserving of his counsel and of his protection upon guidance, since he was the head of the guided, the listener became eager to hear about what came from others. So God, exalted is He, resumed the mention of him with His words: ﴿He said﴾, that is, Musa, upon him be peace, said to the leader of the people of misguidance, turning away from his brother after accepting his excuse, making what had been attributed to him a reason for questioning him about what moved him to do it: ﴿"What is your business?"﴾, that is, what is this strange, great matter which moved you to do what you did, and the Mighty, the All-Knowing, has informed me [that] it is you who led them astray with it, ﴿O Samiri!﴾

Al-Samiri replied to him (Musa), saying: ﴿I saw﴾ from sight (al-basar) and insight (al-basirah) ﴿what they did not see﴾ concerning the matter of the Messenger (al-Rasul) who brought us across the sea. ﴿So I grasped﴾, i.e., so it was [a cause -] that I grasped ﴿a handful﴾, i.e., one time of grasping, and he used it for what was grasped, calling the object by the verbal noun (tasmiyat al-maf'ul bil-masdar) ﴿from the trace﴾ of the horse of that ﴿Messenger﴾, i.e., the well-known one. ﴿Then I threw it﴾ into the jewelry cast into the fire, or into the calf. ﴿And thus﴾, i.e., just as my soul made the taking of his trace attractive to me, ﴿my soul made attractive﴾, i.e., beautified and adorned for me, ﴿casting it﴾ into the jewelry, ﴿so I cast it﴾. Thus there came about what came about, and no caller summoned me to that, nor did any impeller drive me to it except the enticement (al-taswil).

[p. 336] And since his act separated the Children of Israel from the path of truth that they had been following, and gathered them around the image of an animal, one of the basest of animals, and [since] he himself became one who was followed in that misguidance, because he was its cause, he was punished with aversion from humankind, who are the noblest of animals. This was so that his punishment would be a cause for the opposite of what his act had caused. Thus he is punished in this world with a punishment than which none is more severe: he was completely prevented from mixing with people, so that no one associates with him and he associates with no one. Rather, he remains solitary and outcast for as long as he lives. Therefore the report about this is resumed with His saying, exalted is He: ﴿He said﴾, that is, Musa, peace be upon him, said to him: ﴿Go﴾, that is, as a consequence of your deed I say to you: go [away from among us, or -] wherever you go. ﴿For you, in life﴾, that is, as long as you are alive, [there is] ﴿that you say﴾ to everyone you see: ﴿No touching﴾, that is, do not touch me and I will not touch you. So you cannot free yourself from this, by the will of the true God, who wills this for you and makes you desire it, which is what the lam conveys, so that you and those who follow you may know that you were in the greatest error in abandoning the One who has power over all things and in following what has no power over anything. ﴿And indeed for you﴾, after death, ﴿is an appointment﴾ for reward if you repent, and for punishment if you refuse. [p. 337] ﴿You will not be failed in it﴾, read in both the active and passive forms, that is: it will not be behind you, nor will you be behind it. Rather, each of you will face the other, with no escape from him, just as in life you cannot free yourself from aversion to people. So choose for yourself what pleases you.

When he had mentioned the complete power of the true God in both abodes, he followed it with the powerlessness of the calf, and said: ﴿And look at your god﴾, that is, according to your claim, ﴿which you remained﴾, that is, you continued [for a very short period, as indicated by the intensive form of the verb] ﴿devoted to it﴾, that is, turning to it, close to it, persistently [openly -] ﴿We will surely burn it﴾, that is, with fire and with a file, as already mentioned from the text of the al-Tawrah (the Torah). The meaning of this is that he heated it until it softened and became easy to file. ﴿Then We will surely scatter it﴾, that is, We will disperse it [once it becomes dust -] ﴿into the sea﴾, that is, the sea in which [Allah drowned the family of Pharaoh, and -] it is suitable to be the object of such an act. [Allah will gather its dust, which is made from their ornaments and wealth, and heat it in the fire of Hell, brand them with it, and make it among the most severe punishments upon them. He emphasized the verb to show the greatness of Allah who commanded him to do this, and to confirm the truthfulness of the promise, so He said -]: ﴿with a scattering﴾.

Al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on Surah 20, verse 98:

When He showed them the falsity of what they were upon by direct sight, He informed them of the truth in a restrictive manner (ʿalā wajh al-ḥaṣr), saying: ﴿Your God is only Allah﴾, collectively, ﴿Allah﴾, meaning the One who gathers all the attributes of perfection. Then He disclosed the intended meaning of that and affirmed it with His words: ﴿He, there is no god except Him﴾, meaning that none other than Him is fit for this station, because ﴿He has encompassed all things in knowledge﴾. "Encompassed" here is a tamyīz (specifying accusative) transferred from the agent, meaning His knowledge has encompassed every thing, so He is capable over every possible thing, and every thing is in need of Him, while He is independent of every thing. His existence is distinct from the existence of others, His essence is distinct from the essence of others, and His attributes are distinct from the attributes of others. As for the calf they worshipped, even if it were alive it would be a paradigm of stupidity, so it is not fit for divinity in any respect, and there is no right at all in worshipping it. The analogy that comes to mind is that He negated knowledge from it with His words: ﴿Does it not return to them a word?﴾ [Ṭā-Hā: 89], and power with His words: ﴿nor does it possess for them any harm or benefit﴾ [Ṭā-Hā: 89], so that these two would be affirmed here for the true God. But He gave attention to affirming all-encompassing knowledge, because it entails power over everything that can be related to it, by supplying the causes for the desired thing and preventing hindrances from it, so that it occurs necessarily. Had it not been so, failure would result from ignorance, either of what would supply a requirement or of what would prevent an obstacle. The clearest proof of this is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Had I known the unseen, I would have acquired much good, and no harm would have touched me﴾ [al-A'rāf: 188]. Affirming all-encompassing power does not entail comprehensive knowledge, because it excludes the category of the impossible, which is not within the scope of power to relate to.

When this story had been completed in this supreme manner and this most upright way, fulfilling the indication of the good news at the beginning of the surah, that this community would increase and that the Arabs would be turned back from their error after long persistence in obstinacy and deviation from the path of rectitude, and including the consolation through the conditions of the righteous predecessors (al-salaf al-salih) and the encouragement, and detailing the proofs of divine oneness (tawhid) and of resurrection (al-ba'th), along with other wisdoms that stir aspirations toward lofty qualities, it was as if it were said: Is any of the stories to be repeated in this wondrous style and this exalted pattern? It is said: Yes. ﴿Thus﴾, i.e., like this lofty narration, in this precious and mighty composition, concerning the story of Musa and those mentioned with him, ﴿We relate to you﴾, i.e., by means of the greatness We possess, which nothing can overpower. He indicated the sublimity of His knowledge by saying: ﴿from the news﴾, i.e., the reports ﴿of what has passed before﴾ of the times and the great events, as an increase in your knowledge, an exaltation of your rank, a consolation to your heart, and the removal of your grief, through what happened to the messengers before you [and an increase of your followers, and an addition to your miracles, so that the listener may take heed and the one seeking insight may increase in his religion in clear understanding, and the proof may be confirmed against whoever reviles it]: ﴿And We have certainly given you﴾ from Our greatness (p-340), as an honoring of you and an exaltation of your station, ﴿from Ourselves﴾, i.e., from Our presence, a noble matter with greater special closeness to Us and subtle connection to Our presence [from - ] unseen, an unseen (matter) ﴿reminder﴾, great and sublime, comprising what We have manifested of Our command in the Torah, what We have concealed of Our secret in the Gospel, and what We have deposited of Our tranquility in the Psalms, together with what We have specifically granted it of subtle excellences and mighty secrets. It is known by mere recitation that it is from Us, because the spirit bears witness to it, one tastes from it humility and tranquility, and its majesty is seen in hearts, along with certainty that no one can produce its equal. We have included in it those stories, together with what We added to them of admonitions, rulings, and subtle indications of realities, securing the happiness of both abodes and the best of the two bounties. Whoever turns to it, it will remind him of every beneficial knowledge he seeks.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 20, verse 100:

When this Reminder (al-Dhikr) comprised all the doors of good, and everything that has no basis in it was pure wretchedness and far-off misguidance, He said, relating to him news of what is to come just as He related news of what had already passed: ﴿Whoever turns away from it﴾, i.e., from that Reminder, and this is general over all who can be included in the meaning of "whoever" (man) among the worlds, ﴿then he will bear﴾. Since the intended meaning is the encompassing of the time, He said: (p-341) ﴿on the Day of Resurrection a burden﴾, i.e., a heavy load of punishment caused by the burden (wizr), which is the sin, as a recompense for his turning away from it [and his occupation with other than it].

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 20, verse 101:

﴿Abiding therein﴾. He used the plural here, in keeping with the meaning after the singular form of the word, as an alert to the generality (ʿumūm), lest it be overlooked due to the length of the separation, or lest it be assumed that the group could repel it. It is also possible that by "wizr" (burden) is meant a heavy load of sin, and that the pronoun in "fīhi" (therein) refers to the punishment that results from it, making this an instance of istikhdām (a double-meaning usage), as in his saying:

When the rain-cloud descends upon a people's land, we pasture it, even if they are angry.

Since they denied the Day of Resurrection, He mentioned it again explicitly, though the reference was recent, striking their ears with it, and treating it as something deserving of being certain, with no doubt about it. So He said: ﴿And evil it is﴾, meaning "and wretched it is." He then specified the people of evil by saying: ﴿for them﴾, meaning that burden, ﴿on the Day of Resurrection, a burden﴾.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 20, verse 102:

Then he explained to them some of the conditions of that Day from its beginning, saying, substituting from "the Day of Resurrection": ﴿The Day the Trumpet is blown﴾, i.e., by Our majesty — according to the recitation of Abu 'Amr with the nun, in the active voice, and it indicates the perfection of majesty through the manner of speech of the Powerful; in the recitation of the rest with the ya', in the passive voice (p-342) ﴿in the Trumpet﴾, so the dead rise from the graves. ﴿And We gather﴾, i.e., by Our majesty, ﴿the criminals﴾, those among them who severed what God commanded to be joined. He turned away from saying "and We gather them" to clarify the attribute that their turning away from the Remembrance brought upon them. ﴿On that Day﴾, i.e., the Day of Resurrection, and there will be for them what has preceded. ﴿Blue-eyed﴾, i.e., with blue eyes and bodies, in the form of one who has been struck so that his body is changed, while they are in a state of ...

﴿يَتَخافَتُونَ﴾ [They speak in hushed tones].

Since *takhāfut* (speaking in a hushed voice, i.e., confidential speech with lowered tone) may occur between two people from two different tribes, so that each of them is afraid of his own people and considers it less shameful than if they were from the same tribe, [God] indicated that this fear is a constant trait. To show its constancy and generality, He said: ﴿بَيْنَهُمْ﴾ [among themselves], meaning they speak with lowered voices out of awe and dread.

Since blueness was the most disliked eye color among the Arabs [because they were not accustomed to it], and hushed speech was the most disliked kind of voice among them, because in their view it indicates low resolve and cowardice [and they were more averse to blueness because hushed speech may serve some purpose; He, glory be to Him, arranged them in this way], He then explained what they speak in hushed tones, saying: (p-343) ﴿إنْ﴾ [saying that], meaning some of them say to others: ﴿لَبِثْتُمْ﴾ [you remained] in the worldly life [underestimating the length of their stay in the unseen state of what had appeared to them of terrors, or out of error and bewilderment], ﴿إلا عَشْرًا﴾ [except ten], meaning one *ʿaqd* (a single unit of ten), since the number did not exceed the units except by one. This is [even if it were years] the age of one who has not reached puberty, [how much less if it were months or days], so they did not know the pleasure of life under any estimate.

The commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 20, verse 104:

Since knowledge of what is yet to come is more hidden than knowledge of what has passed, [He] used the manifestation of greatness, saying: ﴿We know best﴾ of anyone ﴿what they say﴾, meaning on that day, ﴿when the most exemplary of them in conduct says﴾ in this world, according to what they reckon, [meaning the one nearest to having his conduct be like what is demanded of him]: ﴿You did not remain﴾ [meaning: not] ﴿except a day﴾. [The omitted counted noun in the first part is indicated, by the phrase that follows, to be the days.] That is, the first of the units, not the first of the tens, as He said in the other verse: ﴿They said: We remained a day or part of a day﴾ [Al-Mu'minun: 113]. ﴿The criminals swear that they remained not but an hour; thus were they deluded﴾ [Ar-Rum: 55]. So they remain in delusion and turned away from the truth in both abodes, because a person dies upon what he lived upon and is resurrected upon what he died upon. It is also possible that the meaning is that whoever said their stay was one day is, in reality, the most exemplary of them, because time, however long, is only a recurring day, not intended for its own sake, but intended for what happens within it. If it was good, its owner was praised [and] its shortness did not harm him; if it was evil, its owner was blamed and its length did not benefit him. It is also possible that he used the feminine [in the first part] intending the nights, because they are the place of the rest that is sought in itself.
