It was as if they said: We had no rest except in a very brief time, more than the first of the tens. The most exemplary one specified the day in which the toil is for rest in the night, indicating that they had no rest at all during their stay in the world, and their striving was entirely wretched, as striving is on a day with no night in which one rests. And if there was rest in it, it was incidental, not essential.

When he had reported some of what had already passed, and then some of what is yet to come concerning the states of those who turn away from this Reminder, and what their turning away brings upon them, and had concluded that with their underestimating the length of their stay in this world, he reported some of their states in turning away, saying: ﴿They ask you about the mountains.﴾ What will their condition be on the Day the Trumpet is blown? This is their doubt about the Resurrection, as they stop at the illusion that the mountains will certainly continue to exist, according to the measure of their dullness, because they are the strongest of things, the longest-lasting, and the most enduring in staying. So they prevent some people from hearing the blast of the Trumpet, and to others, through the reflection of the air that carries the sound, it seems to come from other than its true direction, so the aim toward the Caller does not go straight.

﴿So say﴾, i.e., as a consequence of Our knowledge that they will ask you this question (p-345), We say to you: "Say." Or it is conditional, meaning: if they ask you, then say to them. This differs from what was revealed after the question had been asked about it, such as the Spirit and the story of Dhu al-Qarnayn, for the command to answer it comes as a resumptive statement (isti'naf), because of the soul's eagerness (istishraf) for the answer there.

﴿He will blow them away﴾, i.e., He will uproot them from their places and scatter them into the air. ﴿My Lord﴾, the One who is good to me by granting me victory on [the Day of] Resurrection, a victory whose true reality cannot be reached, ﴿a blowing away﴾ at the first blast.

Translation:

﴿So He will leave it﴾, i.e., its places, ﴿a level plain﴾, i.e., a smooth earth, ﴿a flat expanse﴾, i.e., level, as if it were one single row, with no trace of the mountains in it.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 20, verse 107:

﴿You will not see﴾, i.e., with the eye [و -], not with insight, ﴿in it﴾, i.e., in the places of the mountains, ﴿any crookedness﴾ in any way whatsoever. He expressed it here with *'iwaj* (crookedness), which is used for meanings, and did not express it with *'awaj* (crookedness), which is used to describe physical things, although the places of the mountains are physical things and not meanings. This is a negation of crookedness in the most eloquent manner, meaning that if you gathered the people of expertise in leveling land, they would agree on ruling that it is level. Then, if you gathered the people of geometry (*handasa*) and they applied their scientific measurements to it, they would rule the same way. ﴿Nor any elevation﴾, i.e., anything raised up like a mound, or a slight protrusion, or a split [or difference -]. Al-Bayḍawi and al-Zamakhshari said: *al-amt* is a slight protrusion. Al-Ghazali said in *al-Durra al-Fakhira*: (p-346) The Trumpet is blown, the mountains fly off, the rivers burst forth into one another, the world of the air becomes filled [with water -], the stars are scattered, the heavens and the earth change, and the inhabitants of the worlds die, so the earth and the heavens are emptied. He said: Then Glorified is He uncovers a house in Saqar, and the flame of the fire comes forth and ignites the seas, so they dry up. He leaves the earth as a black ember, and the heavens become like the dregs of olive oil and molten copper. Then Exalted is He opens a treasury from the treasuries of the Throne in which is the sea of life, and He rains it upon the earth. It is like the semen of men, so the bodies sprout in their forms: the child as a child, the old man as an old man, and what lies between them. Then a subtle fire blows from beneath the Throne, and the earth is laid bare, with no mountain in it, no crookedness, and no elevation. Then Allah revives Israfil, and he blows into the Trumpet from the Rock of Holiness, and the spirits come out through a hole in the Trumpet, each spirit according to its number, going to its body, even the wild beasts and the birds. Then they are in the *sahira* (the wakeful surface of the earth).

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 20, verse 108:

When He, glory be to Him, had informed of the removal of whatever crookedness might occur in the voice, He said: ﴿On that Day﴾, that is, when the Trumpet is blown and the mountains are scattered, ﴿they will follow﴾, that is, the people of the gathering [with the utmost of their effort], ﴿the caller﴾, that is, the one calling by the blast, standing upright toward him in straightness, ﴿with no crookedness to him﴾, that is, the caller has no deviation in anything of their intention toward him, (p-347) because there is nothing on the earth that would necessitate their swerving aside, and nothing that prevents the voice from reaching everyone equally. Abu Hayyan said: That is, there is no crookedness in his call; rather, it makes all of them hear, so it does not incline toward some people over others.

When He had informed of their humility in speech and their submission to the summons, He informed of the humbling of other voices which customarily accompany gathering, so He said: ﴿And the voices will be hushed﴾, that is, they will be relaxed, lowered, and subdued, and brought low, owing to the humility of their owners ﴿before the Most Merciful﴾, that is, the One whose blessings are general, so His generosity is hoped for and His punishment is feared. ﴿So you will not hear﴾, that is, as a consequence of their subdued state, ﴿except a whisper﴾, the faintest of all sounds. [And it was said: the faintest of the sounds of footsteps.]

[وَلَمَّا تَقَرَّرَ مَا لِلْأَصْوَاتِ -] مِنَ الانْخِفَاتِ [that voices are subdued], وَكَانَ قَدْ أُشِيرَ [فِيمَا مَضَى -] إِلَى وُقُوعِ الشَّفَاعَةِ مِنْ بَعْضِ أَخِصَّائِهِ بِإِذْنِهِ، وَكَانَ الحَشْرُ لِلْحِسَابِ بِمَعْرِضِ التَّقْرِيبِ لِبَعْضٍ وَالتَّبْعِيدِ لِبَعْضٍ، وَكَانَتِ العَادَةُ جَارِيَةً بِأَنَّ المُقَرَّبَ يَشْفَعُ لِلْمُبْعَدِ، لِمَا بَيْنَ أَهْلِ الجَمْعِ مِنَ الوَصْلِ وَالأَسْبَابِ المُقْتَضِيَةِ لِذَلِكَ، وَكَانَ الكُفَّارُ يَزْعُمُونَ أَنَّ آلِهَتَهُمْ تَشْفَعُ لَهُمْ (p. 348) قَالَ نَافِيًا لِأَنْ تَقَعَ شَفَاعَةٌ [بِغَيْرِ إِذْنِهِ -]، [مُعَظِّمًا ذَلِكَ اليَوْمَ بِالإِنْذَارِ مِنْهُ مَرَّةً بَعْدَ مَرَّةٍ -]: ﴿يَوْمَئِذٍ﴾ [أَيْ إِذْ كَانَ مَا تَقَدَّمَ -] ﴿لَا تَنْفَعُ الشَّفَاعَةُ﴾, i.e., there will be no intercession that could benefit, because it has already been established from what came before that there is no [audible] voice, and it has been established in the verification of the universal propositions of the science of logic (ʿilm al-mīzān, the science of the balance, i.e., logic) that a true negative proposition does not require the existence of the subject in external reality. He changed the expression only because the primary intended matter is the benefit, so negating it from the outset is more severe, and the striking of the hearing with it first is more terrifying and frightening. ﴿إِلَّا﴾, i.e., except the intercession of ﴿مَنْ أَذِنَ لَهُ الرَّحْمَٰنُ﴾, the One of all-encompassing grace, ﴿وَرَضِيَ لَهُ قَوْلًا﴾, even if it is merely bare faith (al-īmān al-mujarrad).

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 20, verse 110:

When He negated that intercession could occur without His permission, He gave the reason for that—as was previously stated in the Verse of the Throne (Ayat al-Kursi)—by His saying: ﴿He knows what is before them﴾, that is, the creatures [and this is all that they know —], ﴿and what is behind them﴾, and this is all that is hidden from their knowledge, meaning His knowledge [glorified is He —] encompasses them. So He restrains their hearts on that Day, by means of the causes that come into being, from intending anything He does not approve of. ﴿But they do not encompass Him in knowledge﴾, so that they may guard against what He decrees for them. And ﴿knowledge﴾ (ʿilman) is a specificative (tamyiz) transferred from the subject (al-fa'il), [i.e. —] and their knowledge does not encompass Him—so said Abu Hayyan. The closer view, in my opinion, is that it is transferred from the object to which the verb extends by means of the preposition, i.e. "and they do not encompass His knowledge," and that this is closer to what is in the Verse of the Throne.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 20, verse 111:

When he had mentioned the humbling of voices, he followed it with the humbling of what is beneath them, saying: ﴿And faces will be humbled﴾, that is, they will be abased, submissive and surrendered [the faces of all creation -], and he singled them out for their nobility and because they are the first place where abasement appears. ﴿Before the Ever-Living﴾, who is aware of the subtle and the great, and everything other than Him is inanimate, wherever its life is compared to His life, ﴿the Self-Subsisting﴾, who never neglects the management and the recompense of every soul for what it has earned. ﴿And he has failed﴾, that is, has lost [a manifest loss -] ﴿who carries﴾ [from among them, or from others -] ﴿injustice﴾.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 20, verse 112:

When he had mentioned the wrongdoer (al-zalim), he followed him with the righteous one (al-hakim), saying: ﴿And whoever does⦈ righteous deeds. Since man is a place of incapacity however hard he strives, He said ﴿of the righteous deeds﴾, meaning those which Allah has commanded him to perform according to his capacity, because «No one will ever measure Allah by His true measure» and «No one will ever overburden the religion except that it overcomes him». ﴿while he is a believer﴾, so that its structure is built upon the foundation. [He expressed it with the fa' (so, then) to indicate the acceptance of deeds and making them a cause for that state, and so He said: ﴿then he will not fear injustice﴾ [that a evil he did not commit be attributed to him], because the recompense is of the same kind as the deed. The reading of Ibn Kathir in the prohibitive form (lā yakhaf) confirms the emphasis in negation. ﴿nor deprivation﴾, meaning a diminution of his reward, even though He has not given the station its due, because he is not able to do so. The root of hadm is breaking. As for the non-believer, even if he performed deeds like mountains, they would have no weight for him.

When this verse came to comprise the summit of excellent meanings, bringing glad tidings and facilitation, warning and caution, clarifying what was hidden and revealing what was concealed, together with the grandeur of its composition and the excellence of its arrangement, it was as if it were said, to draw attention to its greatness: We sent it down in this honorable pattern and lofty form. ﴿And thus﴾, that is, and in the manner of this sending down, ﴿We have sent it down﴾, that is, this entire Reminder, by Our greatness, ﴿as an Arabic Qur'an﴾, comprehensive of all the intended meanings, ﴿clarifying what has been deposited in it for everyone who has a taste for the styles of the Arabs.﴾

Since most of these verses are cautionary, He said: ﴿And We have varied﴾, that is, by what We possess of greatness, ﴿in it of the warning﴾, that is, We have mentioned it repeatedly, turned into diverse styles and varied, harmonious arts.

When He mentioned the warning, He followed it with its fruit, saying: ﴿so that they may be mindful of God﴾, that is, so that the one who looks at them afterwards may be hopeful that they will fear God and be among those who renew piety at all times, such that it becomes a continuous attribute for them, which is the caution that prompts taking precautions against what is to be feared. ﴿Or﴾ [that they may be among those] who ﴿renews﴾, that is, renews this variation, ﴿for them a remembrance﴾, that is, something worthy of being remembered of the ways of goodness, so that it becomes a cause of the fear that prompts piety, and thus turns them back from some of the deficiencies and miseries to which the souls incline.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 20, verse 114:

When these sentences reached the peak of inimitability, and encompassed the utmost of wisdom, indicating that their Speaker possesses complete knowledge, power and justice in the affairs of both abodes, there resulted from their being delivered in this manner that there became manifest to Him such greatness as his statement made understood, extolling His Most Holy Self with what He is worthy of, after extolling His Book [to teach His servants what is due to Him of truth], indicating by the form of reciprocity (tafa'ul) an increase in exaltedness: ﴿So exalted is Allah﴾, i.e., [He has reached] the One whom the describers cannot describe as He truly deserves, in an exaltedness that minds cannot grasp; thus nothing of the deviation of the deviators or the descriptions of the polytheists touches Him. ﴿the King﴾, Who is not incapable of anything, so there is in reality no king other than Him. ﴿the Truth﴾, i.e., the One whose dominion is established, so there is no cessation of His being King at any time; and by the greatness of His dominion and the truth of His essence and attributes, He turns His creation over to what they are upon of diverse affairs.

Since these verses were in censure of those who turned away from this Remembrance, the implied meaning is: so do not turn away from it, [but turn towards it] so that you may be among the God-fearing who remember. And since this [great] exhortation may require the one who is eager in piety to exceed in hastening to it, hurrying to seize it before the completion of its revelation, He said, conjoining it to this implied clause: ﴿And do not hasten with the Qur'an﴾, i.e., with its recitation.

Since the prohibition is general for all times prior [to completion], He indicated it by the prepositional phrase, lest it be thought that it is specific to a period that occupies the whole of the prior time [as one unit], so He said: ﴿before its revelation is completed﴾. And since the consideration here is to the completion of the revelation and not to a specific revealer, He put into the passive his statement: ﴿is completed﴾, i.e., is brought to an end, ﴿to you﴾, ﴿its revelation﴾, from the angel descending to you from Our presence with it, just as We did not hasten in sending it down to you all at once, but rather We recited it to you with distinct recitation, and sent it down to you as a gradual sending down, detailed in detail and connected in connection, as We indicated at the beginning of the surah. So listen to it, giving all your attention to it, and do not keep pace with it in recitation. When it has finished, then recite it, for We will gather it in your heart, and We will not cause you to forget it while you are attentive to it, nor by obligating you to keep pace with its recitation.

﴿And say: My Lord﴾, i.e., the One who benefits me by bestowing knowledge upon me, ﴿increase me in knowledge﴾, i.e., by making understood what You have sent down to me of it, and by sending down other than it, just as You increased me by sending it down and making it memorized, so that I may be able to know the causes that bring about the following of creation for you. For as has preceded, the comprehensiveness of power is in proportion to the extent of the encompassing of knowledge. In this there is evidence that deliberateness in knowledge, through reflection and through giving ear, is more beneficial than hurried haste, which tires the heart and clouds the state, and is more helpful to memorization. [For whoever comprehends something with true comprehension memorizes it to the utmost of memorization.]

Al-Tirmidhi, Ibn Majah and al-Bazzar narrated from Abu Hurairah, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) used to say:

"O Allah, benefit me by what You have taught me, teach me what will benefit me, increase me in knowledge, and all praise is due to Allah in every state, and I seek refuge in Allah from the state of the people of the Fire." Cited by Ibn Kathir in his tafsir.

When the Exalted One had established through the story of Musa, peace be upon him, what He had alluded to at the beginning of the surah, namely His forbearance and patience toward His servants and His granting them respite despite their deficiency in forgetting the covenants and breaking the pledges, He followed it with [mention of] the praise of (p-354) this Reminder through which it has reached us, and the censure of whoever turns away from it. He concluded it with what He had enjoined upon him, ﷺ, in matters of prohibition and command. Then the Exalted One followed that with the story of Adam, peace be upon him, as a warning against leaning toward what causes forgetfulness, an exhortation to those who have forgotten to return to obedience to the Most Merciful, and an explanation that this forbearance and respite which He had established is His custom from eternity and His attribute that existed while we were in the realm of non-existence. It also shows that He created man with deficiency. Had He seized them for their sins, He would not have left upon it [the earth] a single creature. So He said, linking it to His words ﴿And thus We have sent it down as an Arabic judgment﴾ [al-Ra'd: 37], or ﴿Thus do We relate to you the news of what has passed before﴾ [Ta-Ha: 99], confirming what had preceded regarding the matter of the Qur'an and what He had pledged concerning it, warning against neglecting that even by way of forgetfulness, and fulfilling what He had promised of relating the accounts of earlier peoples, in a manner that accords with this context: ﴿And We had already taken a covenant﴾ with what We possess of greatness ﴿with Adam﴾, the father of mankind, whom We had informed of many of its [the covenant's] matters in the prohibition against eating from the tree ﴿before﴾, meaning at a time in the past, before those mentioned in this surah whose forgetting and turning away have already been mentioned. ﴿But he forgot﴾ Our covenant and ate from it, though he knew, from that greatness, what should not allow him to forget such a covenant, so emphasized by that majesty. So We counted his committing that prohibited act as a sin committed in forgetfulness, because of the high station he held with Us. Thus it is (p-355) of the category of "the good deeds of the righteous are the misdeeds of those brought near," so how much more so for what is beyond that! ﴿And We did not find﴾ in regard to what We possess of greatness ﴿in him resolve﴾, meaning [a firm purpose, a resolute intention and an executing will with no hesitation in it, like the wills of the angels, peace be upon them; the meaning being that he] did not have Our knowledge attached to that as existing. Nevertheless, We pardoned him and did not remove him from the rank of chosenness.

Since the aim of the surah, as has passed, is to inform of forbearance, patience, gentleness toward the one who is far off, and the capacity to deal with the one who turns away, He mentioned this act of Adam, peace be upon him, in this surah using the term disobedience, while explicitly stating that it was in the manner of forgetfulness. He mentioned it first in summary and then followed it with its detail, so that it would be mentioned twice, as emphasis on the meaning alluded to, as confirmation and as a warning against falling into what is prohibited, and as guidance for whoever is "overcome" by the nature of deficiency to hasten to regret and to take up the means of repentance, so that God may turn to him in repentance as He did with Adam, peace be upon him. So He said:

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar, *The Arrangement of Pearls*) on surah 20, verse 116:

﴿And when﴾, meaning: remember this, and remember when ﴿We said﴾, by what is Ours of majesty, meaning: remember Our saying at that time ﴿to the angels﴾, meaning those disposed to carrying out resolve and determination toward the aim, without any hindrance of hesitation or obstacle of lethargy, ﴿Prostrate to Adam﴾, whom We created with My Hand. We did not command them to this except after We had chosen him, and We knew what would proceed from him, and that this does not detract from the rank of his election, for forbearance and generosity are among Our attributes, and mercy is among Our affairs. So do not despair of Our returning with grace and mercy to those of your people who went to extremes in cutting off from Us, whom We have described as contentious. ﴿So they prostrated﴾ [i.e., the angels] ﴿except Iblis﴾, who attributed to God injustice and a failure of wisdom, so he disbelieved, despaired of mercy, and was stripped of good, so he persisted in misleading creation through deception. It is as if it was said: what was his state in not prostrating? So it was said: ﴿he refused﴾, i.e., he was arrogant toward Adam and disobeyed the command of God.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 20, verse 117:

﴿Then We said﴾ as a consequence of that, after We had shown forbearance toward him and did not hasten to punish him: ﴿O Adam, indeed this﴾ (the Shaytan, who was arrogant toward you) ﴿is an enemy to you﴾ permanently, because arrogance arising from envy does not cease ﴿and to your wife﴾ because she is from you. ﴿So let him not expel you both﴾ meaning: do not give ear to him in any way, lest he expel you both. He directed the prohibition at him while the intended addressees were both of them, as an indication that she has such dignity that she should be protected from being the object of a prohibition. He attributed the expulsion to him to increase the warning and to make the aversion more emphatic, and he added, by way of alerting, ﴿from the Garden﴾, meaning that he will not fall short in harming you both and in intending to bring you down from it.

Since the Exalted had explicitly mentioned her partnership with him in the expulsion, it was known that she shares with him its consequences. Since the woman follows the man, he was the one singled out in this abode for all the toil, striving, defending and herding, and most of his fatigue was in matters concerning the woman, He singled him out for the warning against fatigue for that reason, and counted her fatigue as nothing in comparison with his, and to inform that her affair is in his hand: if he is firm, he will lead her to good, and otherwise she will lead him to harm. He expressed fatigue by ﴿wretchedness﴾ to increase the warning against it, saying: ﴿so you will be wretched﴾, meaning: so you will be weary. He did not intend the wretchedness of the Hereafter, for had he intended it, he would not have entered the Garden after that, because the statement implied after the particle "fa" is a report, and a report is not broken.

Then he gave the reason for his misery, on the assumption of expulsion, by describing it with what is not found elsewhere among the pillars upon which a person's sustenance revolves, namely satiety, quenching of thirst, clothing, and shelter.

Mentioning them by the negation of their opposites, so that they strike his hearing with the names of the kinds of wretchedness against which he had warned him, so that he would become such that he avoids the cause that brings them about out of aversion to them. Then, when the overwhelming power has passed over him, he knows that caution does not avail against decree. So He said: ﴿Indeed, for you﴾, i.e., with Us, ﴿is that you will not hunger therein﴾, i.e., at any time, ﴿nor be naked﴾, so that neither your inner nor your outer self is stripped bare.

Surah 20, verse 119 in al-Biqa'i's Nazm al-Durar:

﴿And that you will not be thirsty therein﴾ (p-358) through the burning of the heart, ﴿nor will you be exposed to the sun﴾. That is, you will not be in a place where the heat of the sun strikes you. The meaning is that no heat will strike you, either inwardly or outwardly.

"So Satan whispered to him" — that is, he followed up our warning with whispering, without any delay in time, to ﴿him﴾, the burnt and expelled one, namely Iblis. That is, he cast into him the secret whisper, by means of what We had enabled him to do, namely to run in this type of [being] in the manner of blood, and to project meanings into his heart. It seems that he used "ilā" (to), because the context is explaining how quickly this kind of [being] accepts deficiencies even when they come to it from afar; or because he did not convey that to him except through his wife, so when mentioning both of them he transitively used the verb with lām. It is as if it was said: what did he insinuate to him? So it was said: ﴿He said, "O Adam"﴾. Then he presented the deceit in the manner of a mere offer, to distance himself from accusation and from suspicion of purpose. He first enticed him with his saying: ﴿"Shall I direct you"﴾, for the soul is intensely eager to know what it does not know. Second, with his saying: ﴿"to the tree of eternity"﴾, that is, the one whoever eats from it will live forever, for a human being loves nothing more than long survival. Third, with his saying: ﴿"and a kingdom that does not decay"﴾, that is, one that never wears out at all. It is as if he had said to him, by the tongue of state or of speech: "Yes." Then he said: "This tree of eternity," pointing to the one he was forbidden from, "there is nothing between you and the everlasting kingdom except that you eat from it."

﴿So they both ate from it﴾, meaning: as a consequence of His command, and immediately after it, they both ate from it, following His word and forgetting what had been covenanted to them. ﴿Then their private parts became apparent to them﴾, because they had broken through the veil of the prohibition and its sanctity, so that what they had been warned against, being removed from what they were in, came to pass. ﴿And they began﴾, that is, they started ﴿to cover themselves with leaves of the Garden﴾, [that is] sewing or joining them together, so as to conceal their nakedness. ﴿And Adam disobeyed his Lord﴾, and although he committed the forbidden act only out of forgetfulness, the greatness of his station and the loftiness of his rank required of him more careful attention, constant vigilance, steadiness of heart and alertness of thought. ﴿His Lord﴾, that is, the One who had bestowed upon him favours that He had bestowed on none of his descendants: creating him with His own hand, commanding His angels to prostrate to him, and taking enmity against whoever was hostile to him. ﴿So he went astray﴾, [from] error (ghiwayah), [which is] misguidance (ad-dalal). For this reason they said: the meaning is that he strayed from the path of rectitude, so he erred in the way of attaining eternity by opposing His command. And he is His chosen one (safiyy), yet He did not remove him from the rank of election, for His mercy is vast, His forbearance is great, and His pardon is all-encompassing. So let not the matter of the stubborn people trouble you, for We are able to turn the hearts of whomever We will among them toward faith, making them the purest of the pure, and to bring forth from the loins of whomever We will among them one whose heart We make a mine of wisdom and knowledge.

Since approval of him (despite this act, in which he hastened to follow the enemy and disobey the Friend, for a thing he had no need of) was very unlikely, God affirmed it (p-360) by indicating it with the particle of delay, saying: ﴿Then his Lord chose him﴾, i.e., the one who showed him kindness; ﴿and turned to him in forgiveness﴾, i.e., as a consequence of the choosing, by returning him to the path of rectitude that he had been upon; ﴿and guided him﴾ by preserving him in that, as is the case with the people of closeness and nearness.

When the abodes of kings cannot bear such a thing, and He, glorified is He, had already shown His special care for Adam, peace be upon him, and the account of his wife and of Iblis had not been mentioned, the listener's soul would not be at rest in its eagerness to hear the rest of the account. So He answered that by saying that He sent him down from his sacred abode, the one who prompts to disobedience and the one who is prompted, even though He had prepared him for it through election (ijtiba'). He said, by way of a resumptive new sentence (istin'af, a sentence that begins a fresh statement answering an implied question): ﴿He said﴾, that is, the Lord whose sanctuary was violated, ﴿Go down from it﴾, you two groups: Adam and his followers, and Iblis, ﴿all of you﴾.

Since the context concerns the occurrence of forgetfulness and the weakening of resolve after a firm covenant, He stirred up resolve and roused determination by mentioning the enmity that gives rise to contention, which spurs on aspirations and stirs up resolutions. In answer to one who might be understood to ask, "In what state will the descent be?", He said: ﴿Some of you are enemies to others﴾. This is true of the enmity of each of the two groups toward the other: the group of Iblis, who are the jinn, toward mankind by misguidance, and the group of mankind toward them by guarding against them through amulets, incantations, and other means, and also the enmity of some members of each group toward some others. ﴿Then if﴾, that is, as a consequence of this, knowledge that no one among you has the power to guard against his enemy except through Me, and that there is no protection for you from My side except following My command. ﴿If there comes to you﴾, that is, O assembly who are the most misguided of those burdened with desires among the accountable, ﴿from Me a guidance﴾ by which you guard yourselves against the enemy's seduction and misleading. ﴿Then whoever follows﴾ — He expressed it with the form "iftaʿala" (the eighth verbal form), which implies exertion and completion of the following that arises from intense concern, ﴿My guidance﴾, which I have granted him from the commands of the Book and the Messenger, supported by the evidence of reason. And because of the expression with the form "iftaʿala", He said: ﴿he will not go astray﴾, that is, by reason of that, from the path of rectitude in this world or in the Hereafter at all, ﴿nor will he be miserable﴾, that is, in anything of his striving in either of them. For misery is the punishment of misguidance, and from its negation follows the negation of fear and grief, but not conversely. Thus this is more eloquent than what is in al-Baqarah, for the thing called to in that surah is worship in general, whereas the context here is for dread and for urging seriousness regarding enmity. ﴿Except as a reminder for one who fears﴾ [Ṭāhā: 3], and for turning to the remembrance ﴿Whoever turns away from it, he will bear on the Day of Resurrection a burden﴾ [Ṭāhā: 100], and for guarding against disobedience even through forgetfulness ﴿so he forgot, and We found in him no resolve﴾ [Ṭāhā: 115].

Al-Razi said in al-Lawami': misery is the servant's separation from God, and happiness is his arrival at Him. Al-Isbahani related from Ibn ʿAbbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, guaranteed that whoever follows the Qur'an will not go astray in this world and will not be miserable in the Hereafter.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 20, verse 124:

﴿And whoever turns away﴾ meaning: acts other than the way of the one who is content, by deliberately abandoning what would benefit him by being close to it, ﴿from My remembrance﴾, which is the guidance, ﴿then indeed for him is⁠﴾ the opposite of that, ﴿a livelihood﴾ which He, glorified is He, belittled by making it feminine, then described with the most dreadful description, and it is a verbal noun in which the masculine, the feminine, the plural and others are alike. So He said: ﴿constricted﴾, meaning possessing constriction, that is, narrowness, because he is upon misguidance, even if he thinks that his state is otherwise, in expansiveness and ease. For his misguidance must bring him to ruin, so it is constricted because it is a cause of narrowness and leads to it, by naming the cause with the name of its effect. Moreover, one who turns away from God does not become sated, nor does he reach a point of contentment. Greed controls him, which never ceases to throw down the heart of one who wishes to increase in this world; stinginess is imposed upon him, which holds back his hand from spending; (he is subject to) the enmity of adversaries and the succession of worries; and, moreover, he does not hope for reward and does not feel safe from punishment. Thus he is in the utmost narrowness because of this, and his concern is always greater than his wealth.

«If the son of Adam had a valley of gold, he would seek a second to it; and if he had two valleys, he would seek a third. Nothing fills the belly of the son of Adam except dust, and God turns in forgiveness to whoever repents.» Agreed upon (by al-Bukhari and Muslim), from Anas, may Allah be pleased with him. Such is the state of one who follows his own desire. As for the one who turns wholeheartedly to the remembrance (of God), he is content and satisfied with what he has, abundant in the remembrance of God, who expands the breasts and illuminates the hearts; he is therefore the most expansive in breadth. So do not be deceived by outward forms, but look to the meanings. (p-363) When He mentioned his state in this world, He followed it with His saying: ﴿And We will gather him on the Day of Resurrection blind﴾. That would be at some point of that Day. Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with him and his father, said: when he comes out of the grave he comes out seeing; then when he is driven to the place of gathering, he becomes blind. Or it may be – and this is the closest understanding of the expression – that it refers to some of the people of misguidance, so that it agrees with His saying ﴿How well they will hear and see on the day they come to Us﴾ [Maryam: 38]. And the hadith of 'Abdullah ibn 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with them both, in the Sahih on this subject: the Prophet (ﷺ) said: «Injustice will be darkness on the Day of Resurrection.»

Then he resumed his speech: ﴿He will say﴾, reminding of the earlier blessing in order to win sympathy, for it is the nature of one who has bestowed a favor that he nurtures it, even if the one upon whom it was bestowed falls short; and this sympathy is at its fullest only while there remains room for reconciliation: ﴿My Lord﴾, that is, O You who have been good to me, who have showered Your blessings upon me, ﴿why have You raised me blind﴾ on this Day, ﴿while I was [once] seeing﴾, that is, in the worldly life, or at the beginning of this Day. So it is as if it were said: "With what was he answered?" And it was said:

(﴿قالَ﴾) His Lord said to him: ﴿Thus﴾, meaning, like this vile act you did in the world. The sense is: just as I said, it was. Then he explained according to the first meaning, and gave the reason according to the second, saying: ﴿Our signs came to you﴾, despite their greatness, which is part of Our greatness, ﴿and you forgot them﴾, meaning you treated them with your turning away from them as one treats a thing that is forgotten and that its owner does not see. You made yourself blind in sight and in insight toward them (p. 364), as He, exalted is He, said: ﴿Those whose eyes were veiled from My remembrance﴾ [al-Kahf: 101]. ﴿And thus﴾, meaning, and like that dreadful forgetting, and He placed the adverbial phrase (zarf) first so that it would bind its sequence to the thing it modifies (al-mazruf) and so that its test of his understanding would be magnified, and said: ﴿This Day you are forgotten﴾, meaning you are left as you are, in blindness and wretchedness, in the Fire, so that you are like a thing that no one sees and no one turns to.

And so We recompense those who transgress [beyond bounds] in pursuing their desires, becoming arrogant toward obeying Our commands, and who did not believe in the signs of their Lord, thereby denying His favor, either by denying [them] or by acting as one who denies.

When he mentioned that this astray person was tormented in the world by hardship (al-ḍankk), and mentioned some of what he has in the Hereafter, he said, swearing an oath concerning his denial: "And the punishment of the Hereafter is surely harsher [than the punishment of this world] in whatever form it may be, and more lasting than it, for the world is a place of cessation and of departure and removal."

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 20, verse 128:

Since what has passed in this surah, and what came before it, of the mention of the fates of the earlier peoples and the accounts of those who denied (the messengers), because of their disobedience to the messengers, is a great cause for insight and clarification, they deserved to be rebuked for their persistence in their blindness. So Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿Has it not guided them﴾, that is, has it not made clear to them, ﴿how many generations We destroyed before them﴾, that is, the abundance of Our destruction of those who came before them, ﴿of the generations﴾, because of their denial of Our messengers, (p-365) while ﴿they walk in their dwellings﴾, and they know their news through inheritance, generation after generation, that We help Our allies, destroy Our enemies, and do whatever We will. The better view is that no object is to be assumed, and the meaning is: has not the guiding clarification come to them? What follows then is a resumptive statement, just as the clarification occurred through His words as a resumptive statement: ﴿Indeed, in that﴾, that is, in that great destruction that recurs among every nation, ﴿are signs﴾, most magnificent in clarity, ﴿for those of understanding﴾, that is, the intellects whose nature is to forbid what does not benefit, let alone what harms. For they indicate, through their recurrence, the power of the Doer, and, through the specification of the disbeliever with destruction and the believer with salvation, the perfection of knowledge [along with -] the generality of power, and that He, exalted is He, does not sanction corruption even if He grants respite, and other matters for one who has a restraint from his intellect.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 20, verse 129:

When He had threatened them with the destruction of those who passed before them, He mentioned the reason for the delay regarding them, conjoining it to what the context has guided one to supply, and it is like saying: "Then if Allah, glory be to Him, willed, He would hasten their punishment." ﴿And had it not been for a word﴾, that is, a great, past, and effective decree ﴿that preceded﴾, that is, in eternity ﴿from your Lord﴾, who accustomed you to goodness, that He deals with forbearance (ḥilm) and deliberation (ana'a), and that He does not uproot your deniers, but rather gives them respite, so that He may turn back whomever He wills (p-366) of them and bring forth from the loins of some of them those who worship Him. This is only out of honour to you and mercy to your community, for, as we said at the beginning of the surah, ﴿We did not send down the Qur'an upon you that you should be distressed﴾ [Ta-Ha: 2], by destroying them, even if they were a stubborn people, nor by anything else. We sent it down only so that your followers would increase, and they would do good deeds, and that would be an increase in your nobility. To this the Prophet ﷺ alludes in his saying: "What I was given was only a revelation which Allah revealed to me, so I hope that I will be the one with the most followers." ﴿would have been an obligation﴾, that is, the punishment would have been a necessary obligation of the greatest necessity for every one who sins at the first sin he commits, because of your nobility with Him and your nearness to Him. And had it not been for a fixed term which He set for everything, the matter would likewise have been so, but His mercy preceded His wrath, so He does not hasten, and He set a term, so He does not seize before it. Each of the preceding of the word and the designation of the term is independently sufficient for respite, so how much more when both are combined. Thus, as a consequence of the knowledge that the appointed term must be fulfilled, however much the disobedient one increases in disobedience, there follows the entrusting of affairs to Allah and the absence of anxiety while awaiting relief. Hence He said:

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 20, verse 130:

﴿So be patient over what they say﴾ of mockery and other things directed at you.

Since patience is very hard on the self and runs against natural inclination, because the self is inclined to deficiencies and filled with whisperings, He commanded it for the sake of one who needs perfection, with that which raises him from the lowest of the body to the highest of the spirit, through the two stations (p-367) of adornment [with perfections and disengagement from base vices. He began with the first because it is the aid to the second, and He mentioned the most noble of adornments -] So He said: ﴿And glorify your Lord with His praise﴾, meaning: busy yourself with what saves you from His punishment and brings you near to His presence, by exalting, free of every imperfection, the One who has done good to you, while praising Him by affirming every perfection. This is to be achieved by praying to Him alone and remembering Him with both kinds of remembrance, without turning to anything else. ﴿Before the rising of the sun﴾ refers to the dawn prayer, ﴿and before its setting﴾ to the afternoon and noon prayers. He changed the construction in His words ﴿and during the hours of the night﴾, meaning its times [plural of inw, with a kasra then a sukun, i.e., an hour], [because worship at that time is more excellent, due to the gathering of the heart, the calm of the person, and being alone with the Lord, since worship at that time is more arduous and more fully within the obligation, and so it is more excellent before God]. ﴿So glorify Him﴾, meaning with the maghrib and 'isha' prayers, signalling the greatness of night prayer. He repeated the command concerning the dawn and afternoon prayers to inform of their increased virtue, since their two times are during the folding and the raising [of the day], so He said: ﴿and at the ends of the day﴾. What I have understood, that this is a repetition of those two, is supported by what is in the two Sahihs from Jarir ibn 'Abdullah al-Bajali, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: "We were sitting with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ when he looked at the moon on the night of the full moon and said: 'You will see your Lord just as you see this moon, without being harmed in seeing Him. So if you are able not to be overcome in a prayer before the rising of the sun and before its setting, then do so.' Then he recited this verse." Otherwise there would be no additional exhortation in the verse specifically to these two. Moreover, the words "hours" and "ends" are suitable for voluntary prayers, including the regular sunnah prayers and others, by night and by day. By mentioning the preposition with the hours, he conveyed partiality, because the night is a place of rest; and he omitted it with the ends so that they could be fully covered by remembrance, because the day is the place of activity and alertness. It is also permissible, and this is better, that what is meant by "before the rising" is the dawn prayer, and what is meant by "before the setting" is the afternoon prayer alone, and by some of the hours the maghrib and 'isha', and he included the preposition because they are two times; and by all the ends the dawn, noon and afternoon prayers, because the day has four ends: its beginning, its end, [the end of] its first half, and [the beginning of] its second half, and all of these are covered by glorification. For this reason he omitted the preposition. As for the first and last, they are with the dawn and afternoon prayers; as for the other two, they are with preparing for the prayer and then the prayer itself. In that case the indication of the virtue of the dawn and afternoon prayers is from two aspects: their being mentioned first and their repetition, and the hadith points to this. If it is intended to include the supererogatory prayers, then the "ends" are taken to mean the hours. And Allah is the Guide.

Since man is naturally prone to forgetfulness, and hope is therefore more dominant in him, He mentioned the reward with the word of expectation, lest he feel secure, so He said: ﴿That you may be pleased﴾, meaning: do this so that you may be hoping that your Lord will be pleased with you and so will grant you satisfaction in this world and the Hereafter, by making your religion manifest and raising your affair, and will not place you in a narrow life in this world or in the Hereafter. This is according to the reading of al-Kisa'i and Abu Bakr from 'Asim with the passive form. The meaning according to the reading of the majority, with the active form, is: so that you may be hoping to be continually pleased in this world and the Hereafter; and you will not be thus unless your Lord has given you everything you aspire to.

[Since the soul is inclined toward lowly things, held captive by what is present of perishable gifts, and since its release from that is what leads to its freedom, which signals the elevation of its aspiration, He said, emphasizing to indicate the difficulty of that—]: ﴿And do not strain your eyes﴾, emphasized for him with the heavy nūn (nūn al-tawkīd al-thaqīla), ﴿your eyes﴾, meaning: do not prolong their gaze after the first glance, which is pardoned, seeking to admire ﴿at what We have given enjoyment to﴾, by what We possess of greatness which the magnifying of Our enemies by it in this worldly life does not diminish, ﴿pairs﴾, meaning: kinds of similar types ﴿of them﴾, meaning: of the disbelievers, ﴿the splendor﴾, meaning: the enjoyment (p-370) ﴿of the life of this world﴾, which they do not benefit from in the Hereafter because they do not spend it in obedience to God's commands. It is a verbal noun (maṣdar) from the sense of the verb, like "I sat sitting" (jalastu quʿūdan). Then He gave the reason for their enjoyment in His words, exalted is He: ﴿so that We may test them therein﴾, meaning: that We may deal with them as one who tests, so that it becomes the cause of their punishment in this world through a constricted life, as mentioned earlier, and in the Hereafter through a painful punishment. Its appearance deceives whoever does not reflect on its meaning with true reflection. So what you are in is better than what they are in. ﴿And the provision of your Lord﴾, which He has made habitual for His friends—and it is in the abode of travel—the sufficient good provision accompanied by success, ﴿is better﴾ than their splendor, because it suffices and does not make one rebellious, and it provides you with what brings you near to His presence so that He exalts you, ﴿and more lasting﴾, for He has granted you success in spending it in obedience, so He has written for you of its reward what He will pay you on the day of need in a manner that no one of creation can enumerate; and the whole world, beyond what is in their hands, will be [less than a drop—] in comparison to His ocean. The attribution of His provision to Himself, rather than their provision to Him, though all is from Him, is for honor. And the expression "your Lord" signals kindness, and it contains an allusion to its prevailing over them and its enduring after them, as is the case with the righteous and the wicked alike.

(p-371) When He commanded the purification of the self (tazkiyat al-nafs), He followed it with the information that purification of others is part of it, because that is a stronger proof of sincerity (ikhlas) and more fitting for deliverance, as indicated by the parable of the ship which the Messenger of God (ﷺ) struck for those who enjoin the good and those who abandon it. He said: ﴿And enjoin your family to prayer﴾, just as your father Isma'il (peace be upon him) did, so that he would lead them to every good: ﴿Indeed, prayer forbids immorality and wrongdoing﴾ [al-'Ankabut: 45]. He did not mention zakat, because it is included in the discouragement (al-tazhid) in the verse preceding it.

Since it is hard on the self and of great benefit, He said: ﴿And be steadfast over it﴾, in the reflexive form (ifti'al), ﴿over it﴾, that is, over performing it, devoting yourself wholly to it, even if it occupies you from some of the affairs of livelihood (al-ma'ash), because ﴿We do not ask you for provision﴾, that is, We do not burden you to seek it for yourself or for others. For the greatness of what is Ours requires that We should not burden you with a matter and then not relieve you of what preoccupies you from it.

Since the self, in its entirety, is directed toward the affairs of livelihood, it is as if it were saying: "From where will provision come?" So He said: ﴿We﴾, in the plural of majesty, ﴿provide for you﴾, for you and for them, what We have decreed for you, from whatever direction We wish, from Our vast dominion, even if it is thought to be far away. Scheming does not benefit in provision. So fear God and be moderate in seeking it, and do not exert yourselves excessively in obtaining it and striving for it, for each of those who is diligent in it and those who are careless about it will obtain neither more nor less than what We have apportioned to him from eternity. (p-372) So the one who is mindful of God, who turns to His remembrance, trusts His promise, and is content and satisfied, is in the widest of ease. The one who turns away, relying on his own striving, is always in toil, hardship, exertion and fatigue. ﴿And the final outcome﴾, that is, the complete one, which in reality is the only true outcome, the praiseworthy good state that follows affairs, that is, will come after them, ﴿is for righteousness﴾, that is, for its people. There is no reliance on provision or anything else that equals prayer. For indeed, "when a matter distressed the Messenger of God (ﷺ), he would turn to prayer." Ahmad transmitted it from Hudhayfah, and al-Baghawi cited it at the end of Surat al-Hijr. Al-Tabarani said in his al-Mu'jam al-Awsat: Ahmad (he is Ibn Yahya al-Halwani) narrated to us; Sa'id (he is Ibn Sulayman) narrated to us, from 'Abd Allah ibn al-Mubarak, from Ma'mar, from Muhammad ibn Hamzah, from 'Abd Allah ibn Salam (may God be pleased with him), who said: "When hardship befell his family, the Prophet (ﷺ) would command them to pray, then he would recite: ﴿And enjoin your family to prayer﴾, the verse."

This hadith is not narrated from 'Abd Allah ibn Salam except by this chain of transmission; Ma'mar alone transmitted it. The hafiz 'Imad al-Din Isma'il ibn Kathir said in his Tafsir (commentary): Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, 'Abd Allah ibn Abi Ziyad al-Qattaran narrated to us, Sayyar narrated to us, Ja'far narrated to us, from Thabit, who said: "When the Messenger (ﷺ) was afflicted by poverty, he would call out to his family: 'O my family! Pray, pray!'" Thabit said: "And when a matter befell the prophets, they turned to prayer." Al-Tirmidhi and Ibn Majah both transmitted it in the book of zuhd (asceticism), and al-Tirmidhi said: "Hasan gharib", from the hadith of 'Imran ibn Za'idah, from his father, from Abu Khalid al-Walibi, from Abu Hurayrah (may God be pleased with him), who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "God, the Exalted, says: Devote yourself to My worship, I will fill your heart with richness and close off your poverty. And if you do not do so, I will fill your heart with preoccupation and not close off your poverty." Ibn Majah transmitted from the hadith of al-Dahhak, from al-Aswad, from Ibn Mas'ud (may God be pleased with him): I heard your Prophet (ﷺ) say: "Whoever makes his worries one worry, the worry of the Hereafter, God will suffice him for the worry of his worldly life. And whoever has his worries scattered among the affairs of the world, God does not care in which of its valleys he perishes." He also transmitted from the hadith of 'Umar ibn Sulayman, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Aban, from his father, from Zayd ibn Thabit (may God be pleased with him): I heard the Messenger of God (ﷺ) say: "Whoever has the world as his concern, God scatters his affairs for him, places his poverty before his eyes, and he will not receive from the world except what has been written for him. Whoever has the Hereafter as his intention, God gathers his affairs for him, places his richness in his heart, and the world comes to him humbled."

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 20, verse 133:

When, in this surah, he had presented what he mentioned of the stories of the earlier peoples and the reports of those who passed away, rebuking thereby Quraysh for their obstinacy, like the Jews, so that they could not deny any part of it or direct any criticism at it, and had interspersed it with wondrous wisdoms and rare admonitions in the most eloquent words, and had concluded that with the greatest summons to taqwa (God-consciousness), he marvelled at them for not submitting to the truth, out of disdain for openly proclaiming falsehood, or out of fear of bad consequences. So he said: ﴿And they say﴾. It is likely that this is coordinated with what is implied within the scope of His words ﴿Has it not become clear to them﴾ [Ta-Ha: 128] up to His words ﴿Indeed, in that are signs﴾ [Ta-Ha: 128], to the effect: "And yet they refused that and did not count any part of it as a sign." ﴿Why does he not﴾, that is, why not and why would he not, ﴿bring us a sign﴾ [that is, Muhammad, the Messenger of God ﷺ] ﴿like the signs of the earlier ones﴾ [that is, like the signs of the former peoples] ﴿from his Lord﴾, the One who has been bounteous to him, ﴿indicating his truthfulness﴾.

Since this implied that they did not count any of these clear proofs, which he had presented to those who came before him, as a sign, out of obstinate denial, they deserved reproach. So he said: ﴿Has it not﴾, that is, has there not come to them of the signs in this Qur'an, of what I have singled you out with, of rulings and wisdoms, in the most eloquent meanings and the most graceful arrangements, that has rendered their eloquent ones incapable and silenced their orators, thereby showing with certainty that it is My speech,

﴿has there not come to them a clear proof of what﴾, that is, the reports ﴿that are in the former scriptures﴾, from the scrolls of Ibrahim, Musa, Isa and Dawud, peace be upon them, in the Tawrah, the Injil, the Zabur and other divine books, ﴿such as the stories of Adam and Musa mentioned in this surah and others, which have been related before, as they are among its people, in aspects that only a few of their most skilled scholars know, without any scholar among them or others having mixed with him, and without any one of them being able to oppose what he brought concerning their stories in the arrangement that yields with certainty that he has no teacher except God, Who sent him, and that what he brought of them is a witness to what is in the former scriptures concerning them with truthfulness, because it is the speech of God. Thus it is a clear proof over the others because of its inimitability (i'jaz). So all divine books are in need of its testimony, as one who argues against another needs the testimony of a proof, and after its inimitability is established, he has no need of anything at all. So it is greater than the signs of all the [prophets] whom they demand the like of, by an incomparable measure.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 20, verse 134:

When it became clear by this that they were attacking with what had no basis of doubt for them at all, he followed it with what did involve some kind of doubt for them, had it occurred. So he said, conjoining [with -] ﴿And had it not been that a word﴾ [Ta-Ha: 129] ﴿And had We destroyed them﴾, treating them according to their disobedience in a manner befitting the dignity of greatness, ﴿with a punishment from before it﴾, i.e., from before this Qur'an mentioned in the preceding verse (p-376) and what is near it, and explicitly in His saying ﴿And do not hasten with the Qur'an﴾ [Ta-Ha: 114], and likewise in the structure of the surah: ﴿We did not send down the Qur'an upon you for you to be distressed﴾ [Ta-Ha: 2]. ﴿They would have said﴾ on the Day of Resurrection: ﴿Our Lord﴾, O You who are characterized by beneficence towards us, ﴿why did You not send﴾, i.e., why not, and why did You not, ﴿to us a messenger﴾, and they indicated His greatness and the loftiness of His rank by the particle of ultimacy, so they said: ﴿to us a messenger﴾, i.e., who would command us to obey You, ﴿so that we would follow﴾, i.e., so that as a consequence we would follow ﴿Your signs﴾ which he would bring to us.

Since their following does not occupy the whole span of the past, they said: ﴿before we are humiliated﴾ by the punishment, this humiliation, ﴿and disgraced﴾ by the sins we committed in ignorance, this disgrace. Therefore We sent you to them and established you as a proof against them. We are gentle with them and We uncover from the hearts of whomever We wish among them the rust that is upon them, through what We send down of the Reminder and renew of the signs, until We make your command true and raise your station [and multiply your followers -] and make victorious your partisans.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 20, verse 135:

When He knew this, that their faith was like something impossible, and their disputation never ends, rather if guidance came to them they found fault with it, and if they were punished before it they complained of injustice, it was as if it were said: "What should I do with them?" So He said: ﴿Say: Each is waiting﴾, meaning, from me and from you, ﴿waiting﴾, meaning, awaiting the good outcome of his affair and the turns of time against his enemy, ﴿so wait﴾, for you are like cattle, having no reflection, and you do not permit what is permissible except when it occurs, ﴿so you will know﴾, meaning, soon, by a promise that has no breaking of it, at the uncovering of the veil, ﴿who are the companions of the path﴾ [meaning, the clear, wide road] ﴿the even﴾, meaning, that has no crookedness nor protrusion in it, so it is by its nature that it leads to the goals.

And since the owner of a thing may not be knowledgeable about the thing, nor act upon what he knows of it, He said ﴿and who is guided﴾, meaning, out of misguidance, so that he attains all that benefits him and avoids all that harms him, we or you? Indeed they knew this with certainty on the day of the conquest of the honored Mecca, and their joy in Islam intensified, and they entered desiring forbearance and generosity, and fearing the sword and retribution. Afterwards they would wonder at their hesitation about it and their aversion from it. The meaning of this is that he (ﷺ) and those who followed him are the happy, the wealthy, the content in this world and the Hereafter, and this is the very meaning of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿We have not sent down the Qur'an upon you that you should be distressed﴾ [Ta-Ha: 2]. Thus the end coincided with the beginning, and it indicates that the great one treats with forbearance and does not hasten. And Allah knows best.
